zh: 2. 最早的辩证法家
en: 2. The First Dialecticians

zh: 在达尔文之后一百多年的今天，“万物皆变”这一观念已在受过教育的人群中被普遍接受。但情况并非一直如此。自然选择的进化论曾不得不与那些捍卫《圣经》观点的人进行一场漫长而激烈的斗争——这些人认为上帝在七天内创造了所有物种，且物种是固定不变的。
en: Over 100 years after Darwin, the idea that everything changes is generally accepted amongst educated people. It was not always so. The theory of evolution by natural selection had to fight a long and bitter struggle against those who defended the biblical view that God created all species in seven days, and that the species were fixed and immutable.

zh: 几个世纪以来，教会主导着科学界，宣称地球是静止的、位于宇宙中心。持不同意见者被处以火刑。
en: For many centuries, the Church dominated science and taught that the earth was fixed at the centre of the universe. Those who disagreed were burnt at the stake.

zh: 然而，即便是今天，“变化”这一概念仍被以片面且肤浅的方式理解。进化被解释为缓慢、渐进的变化，排除了突变的可能性。人们认为自然界中不应存在矛盾，而人类思想中出现的矛盾则被归因于主观谬误。事实上，矛盾在自然界的各个层面比比皆是，并且是所有运动与变化的基础。这一事实早在远古时代就被思想家们所理解。这一观点体现在佛教哲学的某些要素中，也是中国古代“阴阳”原理思想的基础。公元前4 世纪，惠施写下如下文字：“天低如地，山平如沼。正午日落，生时即死。”
en: Even today, however, the idea of change is understood in a one-sided and superficial way. Evolution is interpreted to mean slow, gradual change which precludes sudden leaps. Contradictions are not supposed to exist in nature, and where they arise in human thought are attributed to subjective error. In point of fact, contradictions abound in nature at all levels, and are the basis of all movement and change. This fact was understood by thinkers from the earliest times. It is reflected in some elements of Buddhist philosophy. It underlies the ancient Chinese idea of the principles of yin and yang. In the fourth century BC, Hui Shih wrote the following lines: “The sky is as low as the earth; mountains are level with marshes. The sun is just setting at noon; each creature is just dying at birth.”

zh: 将此与希腊辩证法哲学奠基人赫拉克利特（约公元前544—484 年）的以下片段相比较：
en: Compare this to the following fragments of the founder of Greek dialectical philosophy, Heraclitus (c. 544-484 BC):

zh: 火以气的死亡为生，气以火的死亡为生；水以土的死亡为生，土以水的死亡为生。在我们体内，生与死、睡与醒、年轻与年老，皆为同一事物；二者互换位置，转化为另一者。我们踏入而又不踏入同一条溪流；我们存在，又不存在。
en: Fire lives the death of air, and air lives the death of fire; Water lives the death of earth, earth that of water. It is the same thing in us that is living and dead, asleep and awake, young and old; each changes place and becomes the other. We step and we do not step into the same stream; we are and are not.

zh: 在赫拉克利特那里，爱奥尼亚哲学家们那些相互矛盾的论断首次得到了辩证的表达。“在这里我们看到陆地，”黑格尔评论道，“在我《逻辑学》中，没有哪一条赫拉克利特的命题是我没有采纳的。”
en: With Heraclitus, the contradictory assertions of the Ionian philosophers for the first time are given a dialectical expression. “Here we see land”, commented Hegel, “there is no proposition of Heraclitus which I have not adopted in my Logic.”

zh: 尽管赫拉克利特的重要性不言而喻，但他的哲学思想仅以约130 段残篇的形式流传至今，且采用晦涩的格言体风格。甚至在他生前，赫拉克利特就因其言论晦涩难懂而被称为“晦暗者”。这几乎就像是他刻意选择让自己的哲学难以理解。苏格拉底曾诙谐地评论道：“他所理解的极好，他未理解的他也认为同样极好；但这本书需要一位强健的游泳者。”
en: For all his importance, Heraclitus’ philosophy has only come down to us in about 130 fragments, written in a difficult aphoristic style. Even in his lifetime, Heraclitus was known as ‘the Dark’ for the obscurity of his sayings. It is almost as if he deliberately chose to make his philosophy inaccessible. Socrates wryly commented: “What he understood was excellent, what not he believed to be equally so; but that the book required a tough swimmer.”

zh: 在《反杜林论》中，恩格斯对赫拉克利特的辩证世界观作了如下评价：
en: In Anti-Dühring, Engels gives the following appraisal of Heraclitus’ dialectical world outlook:

zh: 当我们考察并思考广阔的自然界、人类历史或我们自身的智力活动时，起初映入眼帘的是一幅联系与相互作用、排列与组合无休止交织的图景，其中没有任何事物能保持原样、原处和原貌，一切都在运动、变化、产生和消亡。［因此，起初我们看到的是整体图景，其各个部分或多或少仍处于背景之中；我们观察的是运动、转变和联系，而不是那些运动、组合和相互联系的事物。］这种原始的、朴素的但本质上正确的世界观属于古希腊哲学，并由赫拉克利特首次明确阐述：万物既存在又非存在，因为万物皆如流水，不断变化，不断生成与消亡。
en: When we consider and reflect upon nature at large or the history of mankind or our own intellectual activity, at first we see the picture of an endless entanglement of relations and reactions, permutations and combinations, in which nothing remains what, where and as it was, but everything moves, changes, comes into being and passes away. [We see, therefore, at first the picture as a whole, with its individual parts still more or less kept in the background; we observe the movements, transitions, connections, rather than the things that move, combine and are connected.] This primitive, naive but intrinsically correct conception of the world is that of ancient Greek philosophy, and was first clearly formulated by Heraclitus: everything is and is not, for everything is fluid, is constantly changing, constantly coming into being and passing away.

zh: 赫拉克利特生活在公元前五世纪动荡不安的以弗所，那是一个战乱频仍、内乱不断的时期。关于他的生平所知甚少，只知道他出身于一个贵族家庭。但他所处时代的本质在他的一段残篇中得到了很好的体现：
en: Heraclitus lived in Ephesus in the violent period of the fifth century BC, a period of war and civil strife. Little is known of his life, except that he came from an aristocratic family. But the nature of the period in which he lived is well reflected in one of his fragments:

zh: 战争是一切事物的父亲，也是万物的君王；它使一些人成为神，一些人成为凡人，使一些人成为奴隶，一些人获得自由。
en: War is the father of all things and the king of all; and some he has made gods and some men, some bond and some free.

zh: 但赫拉克利特在此所指的不仅是人类社会中的战争，还包括自然界各个层面内在矛盾所起的作用。事实上，将其译为“纷争”更为贴切。他指出：
en: But Heraclitus here does not just refer to war in human society, but to the role of inner contradiction at all levels of nature as well. Indeed, it is better translated as ‘strife’. He states that:

zh: 我们必须明白，战争是万物共有的，纷争即是正义，万物皆通过纷争而生灭。
en: We must know that war is common to all and strife is justice, and that all things come into being and pass away through strife.

zh: 万物皆蕴含着矛盾，正是这种矛盾推动着它们的发展。事实上，若无矛盾，便不会有运动，也不会存在生命。
en: All things contain a contradiction, which impels their development. Indeed, without contradiction, there would be no movement and no life.

zh: 赫拉克利特是最早对“对立统一”这一思想进行清晰阐述的人。
en: Heraclitus was the first to give a clear exposition of the idea of the unity of opposites.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学派曾制定了一份包含十组对立面的表格：
en: The Pythagoreans had worked out a table of ten antitheses:

zh: 1. 有限与无限
2. 奇数与偶数
3. 一与多
4. 右与左
5. 男性与女性
6. 静与动
7. 直与曲
8. 光明与黑暗
9. 善与恶
10. 正方形与平行四边形
en: 1. The finite and the infinite
2. The odd and the even
3. The one and the many
4. The right and the left
5. The male and the female
6. The quiescent and the moving
7. The straight and the crooked
8. Light and darkness
9. Good and evil
10. The square and the parallelogram

zh: 这些都是重要的概念，但毕达哥拉斯学派却没有将它们进一步发展，该学派仅满足于对这些概念的简单罗列。事实上，毕达哥拉斯学派主张通过“中道”来融合对立面，即通过寻求中间立场来消除矛盾。赫拉克利特在反驳这一观点时，运用了一个极为鲜明而优美的意象：
en: These are important concepts, but they were not developed by the Pythagoreans, who satisfied themselves with a mere enumeration. In fact, the Pythagoreans had the position of the fusion of opposites through a ‘mean’, eliminating contradiction by seeking the middle ground. Polemicising against this view, Heraclitus uses a most striking and beautiful image:

zh: 人们并不明白，相互矛盾的事物如何能自成一体。这是一种对立张力的协调，就像弓和里拉琴各自体现的协调一样。
en: Men do not know how what is at variance agrees with itself. It is an attunement of opposite tensions, like that of the bow and the lyre.

zh: 矛盾是一切事物的根源。想要消除矛盾，实际上就预设了消除一切运动和生命，因此：
en: Contradiction lies at the root of everything. The desire to eliminate contradiction would actually presuppose the elimination of all movement and life, consequently:

zh: 荷马说：“但愿争斗从神与人之间消失！”这是错误的。他没有意识到，自己是在祈求宇宙的毁灭；因为，如果他的祈祷被应允，万物都将消逝……
en: Homer was wrong in saying: “Would that strife might perish from among gods and men!” He did not see that he was praying for the destruction of the universe; for, if his prayer were heard, all things would pass away…

zh: 这些思想虽深邃，却显然与日常经验和“常识”相悖。一件事物如何能同时既是它自身，又是其他事物？一件事物如何能既活着又死了？对于这种论调，赫拉克利特嗤之以鼻：
en: These are profound thoughts, but are clearly at variance to everyday experience and ‘common sense’. How can something be itself and something else at the same time? How can a thing be both alive and dead? On this kind of argument, Heraclitus poured scorn:

zh: 明智之举是倾听——不是听我，而是听我的“道”，并承认万物皆为一体……尽管这一“道”永远真实，但人们初次听到它时，却如同从未听过一般无法理解。因为，尽管万物皆依此“道”而发生，当人们尝试我所阐述的言行——将万物按其种类划分并揭示其真实本质时——他们却似乎对此毫无体验。但另一些人在醒着时却不知自己在做什么，正如他们会忘记自己在睡梦中的所作所为……愚人即便听见，也如同聋子一般；那句谚语正是对他们的见证：他们虽在场，却心不在焉……若人的灵魂无法理解感官的语言，那么眼睛和耳朵对他们而言便是不可靠的见证。
en: It is wise to hearken, not to me, but to my Word, and to confess that all things are one… Though this Word is true evermore, yet men are unable to understand it when they hear it for the first time as before they have heard it at all. For, though all things come to pass in accordance to this Word, men seem as if they have no experience of them, when they make trial of words and deeds such as I set forth, dividing each thing according to its kind and showing how it truly is. But other men know not what they are doing when they awake, even as they forget what they do in sleep… Fools when they do hear are like the deaf; of them does the saying bear witness that they are absent when present… Eyes and ears are bad witnesses to men if they have souls that understand not their language.

zh: 这是什么意思？“道”的希腊语是“Logos”，逻辑一词即由此衍生。尽管看似神秘，赫拉克利特的开篇之语实则是在呼吁理性的客观性。他在说：不要听我的，而要听我所描述的自然客观法则。这就是其本质含义。而“万物皆一”又意味着什么？在整个哲学史上，对现实有两种解释方式——要么将其视为一种单一的实体，以不同的形式体现（一元论，源自希腊语中“单一”之意）；要么将其视为两种截然不同的实体，即精神与物质（即二元论）。早期希腊哲学家是唯物主义的一元论者。后来，毕达哥拉斯学派基于心灵（精神）与物质之间所谓不可逾越的鸿沟，采纳了二元论立场。这是所有唯心主义的标志。正如我们所见，其根源在于野蛮人的原始迷信——他们相信灵魂会在梦中离开身体。
en: What does this mean? The Greek for Word is ‘Logos’, from which logic is derived. Despite its mystical appearance, Heraclitus’ opening remark is an appeal to rational objectivity. Do not listen to me, he is saying, but to the objective laws of nature which I describe. That is the essential meaning. And “all things are one”? Throughout the history of philosophy, there have been two ways of interpreting reality – either as one single substance, embodied in different forms (monism, from the Greek word meaning single); or as two entirely different substances, spirit and matter (known as dualism). The early Greek philosophers were materialist monists. Later, the Pythagoreans adopted a dualist position, based upon a supposedly unbridgeable gulf between mind (spirit) and matter. This is the hallmark of all idealism. As we have seen, it has its roots in the primitive superstitions of savages who believed that the soul left the body in dreams.

zh: 上述段落是对毕达哥拉斯学派哲学二元论的论战，赫拉克利特捍卫了早期爱奥尼亚一元论的立场——即自然界存在一种根本的物质统一性。宇宙并非被创造出来的，而是自古以来就存在，处于持续流变与变化的过程中，万物由此转变为其对立面，原因变成结果，结果又变成原因。因此，矛盾是万物的根源。为了探求真理，必须超越表象，揭示特定现象内在的矛盾趋势，从而理解其内在的驱动力。
en: The above passage is a polemic against the philosophical dualism of the Pythagoreans, against which Heraclitus defends the position of earlier Ionic monism – that there is an underlying material unity of nature. The universe has not been created, but has always existed, in a process of continuous flux and change, whereby things change into their opposites, cause becomes effect, and effect cause. Thus, contradiction lies at the root of everything. In order to get at the truth, it is necessary to go beyond the appearances, and lay bare the inner conflicting tendencies of a given phenomenon, in order to understand its inner motive forces.

zh: 相比之下，普通人的思维往往满足于表面现象，对感官知觉所呈现的现实、所谓“所与”和“事实”不加思索地全盘接受。然而，这种认知充其量是有限的，甚至可能成为无尽谬误的根源。仅举一例：在“常识”看来，世界是平的，太阳绕着地球转。事物的真实本质并非总是显而易见。正如赫拉克利特所言：“自然喜欢隐藏。”为了抵达真理，必须懂得如何解读感官信息。“如果你不期待意料之外之事，你就无法发现它，”他写道，并再次指出：“那些寻找黄金的人，挖出许多泥土，却只找到一点点。”
en: The ordinary intelligence, by contrast, is content to take things at face value, the reality of sense perception, the ‘given’, the ‘facts’, are accepted without more ado. However, such perception is at best limited, and can be the source of endless errors. To give just one example: for ‘sound common sense’, the world is flat and the sun goes around the earth. The true nature of things is not always evident. As Heraclitus puts it: “Nature loves to hide.” In order to arrive at the truth, it is necessary to know how to interpret the information of the senses. “If you do not expect the unexpected, you will not find it”, he wrote, and again: “Those who seek for gold dig up much earth and find a little.”

zh: “万物皆流”，这是他哲学的基础。“人不能两次踏入同一条河流；因为新鲜的河水正不断涌向你。”
这是对宇宙的一种动态看法，与毕达哥拉斯学派静态的唯心主义观念截然相反。当赫拉克利特追随泰勒斯和阿那克西美尼的脚步，寻找支撑宇宙的物质实体时，他选择了那种最难以捉摸且转瞬即逝的元素——火。
en: “Everything flows,” was the basis of his philosophy. “You cannot step twice into the same river; for fresh waters are ever flowing in upon you.”

This was a dynamic view of the universe, the exact opposite of the static idealist conception of the Pythagoreans. And when Heraclitus looked for a material substance to underpin the universe, following in the footsteps of Thales and Anaximenes, he chose that most elusive and fleeting element, fire.

zh: 万物处于不断流变之中，除了运动与变化之外，没有任何事物是固定和永恒的——这一观念对于普通人的思维方式来说难以接受。人类的思维，总体而言，天生就是保守的。那种渴望紧抓坚实、具体且可靠事物的愿望，植根于一种深层本能，类似于自我保全的本能。对来世的期盼、对不朽灵魂的信仰，源于对“万物皆生，万物皆亡”——“panta rhei”（万物皆流）这一事实的抗拒。人类顽固地试图通过否认自然法则、为自己虚构某些特权来获得自由。然而，正如黑格尔所阐释的，真正的自由在于正确理解这些法则，并据此行事。赫拉克利特所发挥的伟大作用，在于首次提供了关于辩证世界观的、或多或少较为完整的图景。
en: The idea that everything is in a constant state of flux, that there is nothing fixed and permanent except motion and change, is an uncomfortable one for the ordinary cast of mind to accept. Human thinking is, in general, innately conservative. The desire to cling to what is solid, concrete and reliable is rooted in a profound instinct, akin to that of self-preservation. The hope for an afterlife, the belief in an immortal soul, flows from a rejection of the fact that all things come into existence and also pass away – ‘panta rhei’, everything flows. Man has stubbornly sought to attain freedom by denying the laws of nature, inventing certain imaginary privileges for himself. True freedom, however, as Hegel explained, consists in correctly understanding these laws, and acting accordingly. It was the great role of Heraclitus to provide the first more or less fully worked-out picture of the dialectical world outlook.

zh: 赫拉克利特的哲学甚至在他生前就遭到了怀疑和敌视。它不仅挑战了所有宗教和传统的假设，也挑战了那种目光短浅的“常识”思维。在随后的2500 年里，人们一直试图推翻这一理论。正如英国哲学家伯特兰·罗素所评论的：
en: Heraclitus’ philosophy was greeted by incredulity and hostility even in his own lifetime. It challenged the assumptions, not only of all religion and tradition, but of the ‘common sense’ mentality which sees no further than the end of its nose. For the next 2,500 years, attempts have been made to disprove it. As the British philosopher Bertrand Russell comments:

zh: 科学与哲学一样，都试图通过在不断变化的现象中寻找某种恒常的基质，从而摆脱“万物流变”的学说。化学似乎满足了这一渴望。人们发现，看似具有破坏性的火，其实只是将物质转化：元素重新组合，但在燃烧过程中，燃烧前存在的每个原子在过程完成后依然存在。因此，人们认为原子是不可毁灭的，物理世界中的所有变化仅仅是持久元素的重新排列。这一观点一直占主导地位，直到放射性被发现，人们才意识到原子会发生衰变。

物理学家们并未因此气馁，而是提出了构成原子的新的、更小的单位——电子和质子，并曾有数年时间认为这些基本单位具备了此前归属于原子的不可毁灭性。遗憾的是，质子和电子似乎能够相互碰撞并发生爆炸，形成的并非新物质，而是以光速在宇宙中传播的能量波。能量不得不取代物质，成为永恒的存在。但能量与物质不同，它并非对“事物”这一常识概念的细化；它仅仅是物理过程的一种特征。人们或许会天马行空地将其等同于赫拉克利特的“火”，但它只是燃烧的过程，而非被燃烧之物。“被燃烧之物”已从现代物理学中消失。
从微观转向宏观，天文学不再允许我们将天体视为永恒的存在。行星诞生于太阳，而太阳则诞生于星云。它已经存在了一段时间，还将继续存在一段时间；但迟早——大概在一百万百万年后——它会发生爆炸，摧毁所有的行星。至少天文学家是这么说的；也许随着那致命之日的临近，他们会在自己的计算中发现某些错误。
en: Science, like philosophy, has sought to escape from the doctrine of perpetual flux by finding some permanent substratum amid changing phenomena. Chemistry seemed to satisfy this desire. It was found that fire, which appears to destroy, only transmutes: elements are recombined, but each atom that existed before combustion still exists when the process is completed. Accordingly it was supposed that atoms are indestructible, and that all change in the physical world consists merely in re-arrangement of persistent elements. This view prevailed until the discovery of radioactivity, when it was found that atoms could disintegrate.

Nothing daunted, the physicists invented new and smaller units, called electrons and protons, out of which atoms were composed; and these units were supposed, for a few years, to have the indestructibility formerly attributed to atoms. Unfortunately it seemed that protons and electrons could meet and explode, forming, not new matter, but a wave of energy spreading through the universe with the velocity of light. Energy had to replace matter as what is permanent. But energy, unlike matter, is not a refinement of the common-sense notion of a ‘thing’; it is merely a characteristic of physical processes. It might be fancifully identified with the Heraclitean Fire, but it is the burning, not what burns. ‘What burns’ has disappeared from modern physics.

Passing from the small to the large, astronomy no longer allows us to regard the heavenly bodies as everlasting. The planets came out of the sun, and the sun came out of a nebula. It has lasted some time, and will last some time longer; but sooner or later – probably in about a million million years – it will explode, destroying all the planets. So at least the astronomers say; perhaps as the fatal day draws nearer they will find some mistake in their calculations.
body.review: 本段为原书转引罗素的历史文字；质子与电子、行星起源及太阳寿命的表述均照底本保留，不作为当前科学结论。

zh: 埃利亚学派
en: THE ELEATICS

zh: 过去人们认为，赫拉克利特的哲学是对巴门尼德（约公元前540—470 年）观点的一种反拨。如今的主流观点恰恰相反，认为埃利亚学派是对赫拉克利特思想的反拨。埃利亚学派试图通过主张与其截然相反的观点——即万物不变，运动只是幻象——来反驳“万物流动”的观点。这很好地体现了演变过程的辩证性质。一般而言，人类思想的发展，尤其是哲学史的发展，并非沿直线展开，而是通过矛盾不断发展：一种理论被提出后，会受到与其对立的理论的挑战，直到该理论又被新的理论所推翻——而新理论的出现往往看似意味着回归起点。然而，这种看似回归旧观念的现象，并不意味着思想发展仅仅是一个封闭的循环。恰恰相反，辩证过程绝不会以完全相同的方式重复，因为科学争论、讨论以及对立场的不断重新审视——这些过程都以观察和实验为依据——会促使我们的理解不断深化，并使我们更接近真理。
en: In the past it was thought that Heraclitus’ philosophy was a reaction against the views of Parmenides (c. 540-470 BC). The prevailing opinion now is that, on the contrary, the Eleatic school represented a reaction against Heraclitus. The Eleatics attempted to disprove the idea that ‘everything flows’ by asserting the direct opposite: that nothing changes, that movement is an illusion. This is a good example of the dialectical character of the evolution of human thought in general, and the history of philosophy in particular. It does not unfold in a straight line, but develops through contradiction, where one theory is put forward, is challenged by its opposite, until this, in turn, is overturned by a new theory, which frequently appears to signify a return to the starting point. However, this apparent return to old ideas does not mean that intellectual development is merely a closed circle. On the contrary, the dialectical process never repeats itself in exactly the same way, since the very process of scientific controversy, discussion, constant re-examination of positions, backed up by observation and experiment, leads to a deepening of our understanding and a closer approximation to the truth.

zh: 埃利亚（或维利亚）是位于意大利南部的一座希腊殖民地，约于公元前540 年由逃离波斯入侵爱奥尼亚的移民建立。据传统说法，埃利亚学派由克塞诺芬尼创立。然而，他与该学派的关联尚不明确，且其贡献被该学派最杰出的代表——巴门尼德和芝诺（生于公元前460 年）所掩盖。毕达哥拉斯学派从物质中抽去除数以外的一切确定属性，而埃利亚学派则更进一步，将这一过程推向极致，最终形成了一种完全抽象的“存在”概念——这种概念剥离了除纯粹存在之外的所有具体表现形式。唯有“存在”是真实的；“非存在”（即“生成”）则根本不存在：纯粹、无限、不变、无特征的“存在”——这正是埃利亚思想的本质。
en: Elia (or Velia) was a Greek colony in southern Italy founded about 540 BC by emigrants fleeing from the Persian invasion of Ionia. According to tradition, the Eleatic school was founded by Xenophones. However, his connection with the school is unclear, and his contribution was overshadowed by its most prominent representatives, Parmenides and Zeno (born 460 BC). Whereas the Pythagoreans abstracted from matter all determinate qualities except number, the Eleatics went one step further, taking the process to an extreme, arriving at a totally abstract conception of being, stripped of all concrete manifestations except bare existence. Only being is; non-being (becoming) is not at all: pure, unlimited, unchanging, featureless being – this is the essence of the Eleatic thought.
body.review: 英文底本人名拼作Xenophones，译文沿用同书前文的克塞诺芬尼；芝诺出生年份照原书保留。

zh: 这种宇宙观旨在消除一切矛盾、一切可变性和运动。在其自身的参照框架内，这是一种非常自洽的哲学。唯有一处绊脚石：它与整个人类的经验直接相悖。不过这并未让巴门尼德感到担忧。如果人类的理解力无法把握这一理念，那也是理解力的损失罢了！芝诺提出了一系列著名的悖论，旨在证明运动的不可能性。据传说，犬儒学派的第欧根尼仅凭在房间里来回走动，就驳倒了芝诺的论点！然而，正如几代逻辑学家所痛切体会到的那样，在理论层面上要驳斥芝诺的论点并非易事。
en: This view of the universe is designed to eliminate all contradictions, all mutability and motion. It is a very consistent philosophy, within its own frame of reference. There is only one snag. It is directly contradicted by the whole of human experience. Not that this worried Parmenides. If human understanding cannot grasp this idea, so much the worse for understanding! Zeno elaborated a famous series of paradoxes designed to prove the impossibility of movement. According to legend, Diogenes the Cynic disproved Zeno’s argument by simply walking up and down the room! However, as generations of logicians have found to their cost, Zeno’s arguments are not so easy to dispose of in theoretical terms.

zh: 黑格尔指出，芝诺的真正意图并非否认运动的现实性，而是要揭示运动中存在的矛盾，以及这种矛盾在思想中的反映。从这个意义上说，埃利亚学派——尽管听起来有些矛盾——也是辩证法哲学家。在为芝诺辩护、反驳亚里士多德关于他否认运动存在的批评时，黑格尔解释道：
en: Hegel points out that the real intention of Zeno was not to deny the reality of motion, but to bring out the contradiction present in movement, and the way it is reflected in thought. In this sense, the Eleatics were, paradoxically, also dialectical philosophers. Defending Zeno against Aristotle’s criticism that he denied the existence of motion, he explains:

zh: 关键不在于运动是否存在以及这一现象是否存在；运动的存在与大象的存在一样，是感性上确凿无疑的；芝诺并非在此意义上否认运动。问题的关键在于其真理性。然而，运动被认为是不真实的，因为对其的构想包含着矛盾；他以此意在表明，无法将任何真实的“存在”归于它。
en: The point is not that there is movement and that this phenomenon exists; the fact that there is movement is as sensuously certain as that there are elephants; it is not in this sense that Zeno meant to deny movement. The point in question concerns its truth. Movement, however, is held to be untrue, because the conception of it involves a contradiction; by that he meant to say that no true Being can be predicated of it.

zh: 要驳斥芝诺的论点，仅像第欧根尼那样通过四处走动来证明运动的存在是不够的。必须从他自己的前提出发，穷尽他对运动的分析，将其推向极限，直至其转化为自身对立面。这才是辩证论证的真正方法，而非仅仅断言相反的结论，更不应诉诸嘲讽。事实上，芝诺悖论确实有其理性依据，这无法通过形式逻辑的方法来解决，而只能通过辩证法来解决。
en: In order to disprove Zeno’s argument, it is not enough to demonstrate that movement exists, as Diogenes did, just by walking around. It is necessary to proceed from his own premises, to exhaust his own analysis of motion, and carry it to its limits, to the point where it turns into its opposite. That is the real method of dialectical argument, not merely asserting the opposite, still less resorting to ridicule. And, in fact, there is a rational basis for Zeno’s paradoxes, which cannot be resolved by the method of formal logic, but only dialectically.

zh: “迅捷的阿基里斯”
en: ‘ACHILLES THE SWIFT’

zh: 芝诺曾以多种方式“证伪”运动。例如，他论证道：一个运动中的物体在到达某一点之前，必须先走完一半的距离。但在那之前，它必须先走完那一半的一半，如此无限循环往复。因此，当两个物体沿同一方向运动，且后面的物体起初与前面的物体相隔一定距离，且运动得更快时，我们通常认为它会追上前面那个。但芝诺指出并非如此：“较慢者绝不可能被较快者超越。”
这就是著名的“迅捷的阿基里斯”悖论。设想阿基里斯与一只乌龟进行赛跑。假设阿基里斯的奔跑速度是乌龟的十倍，而乌龟拥有1,000 米的领先优势。当阿基里斯跑完1,000 米时，乌龟将领先100 米；当阿基里斯跑完这100 米时，乌龟将领先1 米；当他跑完这一段距离时，乌龟将领先十分之一米，如此循环往复，直至无穷。
en: Zeno ‘disproved’ motion in different ways. Thus, he argued that a body in motion, before reaching a given point, must first have travelled half the distance. But, before this, it must have travelled half of that half, and so on ad infinitum. Thus, when two bodies are moving in the same direction, and the one behind at a fixed distance from the one in front is moving faster, we assume that it will overtake the other. Not so, says Zeno: “The slower one can never be overtaken by the quicker.”

This is the famous paradox of Achilles the Swift. Imagine a race between Achilles and a tortoise. Suppose that Achilles can run ten times faster than the tortoise which has a 1,000 metre head start. By the time Achilles has covered 1,000 metres, the tortoise will be 100 metres ahead; when Achilles has covered that 100 metres, the tortoise will be one metre ahead; when he covers that distance, the tortoise will be one-tenth of a metre ahead, and so on to infinity.
body.review: 原文由领先100米直接写到1米，译文照录。按本段十倍速度的设定，阿基里斯再跑100米时，乌龟应再前进10米，故该步应为领先10米，下一步才为1米。

zh: 从日常常识的角度来看，这似乎荒谬。当然，阿基里斯会追上乌龟！亚里士多德指出：“这一证明同样主张无限可分性，但它是错误的，因为如果允许快速物体穿越既定的距离，它终将追上缓慢的物体。”
en: From the standpoint of everyday common sense, this seems absurd. Of course Achilles will overtake the tortoise! Aristotle remarked that: “This proof asserts the same endless divisibility, but it is untrue, for the quick will overtake the slow body if the limits to be traversed be granted to it.”

zh: 黑格尔引用了这些话，并评论道：
en: Hegel quotes these words, and comments:

zh: 这一回答是正确的，且已涵盖了所有可说的内容；也就是说，在这个表述中存在两个时间段和两个距离，它们彼此分离，即它们彼此限定……
en: This answer is correct and contains all that can be said; that is, there are in this representation two periods of time and two distances, which are separated from one another, i.e. they are limited in relation to one another…

zh: 但他随后又补充道：
en: But then he adds:

zh: ……相反，当我们承认时间与空间作为连续体相互关联时，它们虽为二，却非二，而是同一的。
en: …when, on the contrary, we admit that time and space are related to one another as continuous, they are, while being two, not two, but identical.

zh: 芝诺悖论并未证明运动是一种幻觉，也未证明阿基里斯实际上无法追上乌龟，但它们确实精彩地揭示了如今被称为“形式逻辑”的思维方式的局限性。像埃利亚学派那样试图从现实中消除一切矛盾，不可避免地会导致这种无法解决的悖论，或者如康德后来所称的“二律背反”。为了证明一条直线不可能由无限多个点组成，芝诺声称，如果真是如此，那么阿基里斯就永远无法追上乌龟。这里确实存在一个逻辑问题。正如阿尔弗雷德·胡珀所解释的：
en: The paradoxes of Zeno do not prove that movement is an illusion, or that Achilles, in practice, will not overtake the tortoise, but they do reveal brilliantly the limitations of the kind of thinking now known as formal logic. The attempt to eliminate all contradiction from reality, as the Eleatics did, inevitably leads to this kind of insoluble paradox, or antinomy, as Kant later called it. In order to prove that a line could not consist of an infinite number of points, Zeno claimed that, if it were really so, then Achilles would never overtake the tortoise. There really is a logical problem here. As Alfred Hooper explains:

zh: 即使那些知道可以求出无穷等比级数之和的人，也会被这个悖论所困惑——该级数的公比小于1，其各项因此越来越小，从而“收敛”到某个极限值。
en: This paradox still perplexes even those who know that it is possible to find the sum of an infinite series of numbers forming a geometrical progression whose common ratio is less than 1, and whose terms consequently become smaller and smaller and thus ‘converge’ on some limiting value.
body.review: 此处引文以公比小于1描述收敛条件，按原文保留；一般实数等比级数的收敛条件为公比绝对值小于1。

zh: 事实上，芝诺揭示了数学思维中的一种矛盾，而这一矛盾直到2000 年后才得到解决。这种矛盾与“无限”概念的使用有关。从毕达哥拉斯一直到17 世纪微积分的发现，数学家们不遗余力地避免使用“无限”这一概念。唯有伟大的天才阿基米德曾触及这一主题，但他仍通过迂回的方法来规避它。
en: In fact, Zeno had uncovered a contradiction in mathematical thought which would have to wait 2,000 years for a solution. The contradiction relates to the use of the infinite. From Pythagoras right up to the discovery of the differential and integral calculus in the seventeenth century, mathematicians went to great lengths to avoid the use of the concept of infinity. Only the great genius Archimedes approached the subject, but still avoided it by using a roundabout method.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学派偶然发现，2 的平方根无法用一个数表示。他们发明了巧妙的方法来求其逐次近似值。但无论这个过程进行到何种程度，你永远无法得到精确的答案。结果总是处于两个数的中间。你进行的迭代次数越多，就越接近2 的平方根的值。但这种逐次逼近的过程可以无限延续下去，却无法得到一个可以用整数表示的精确结果。
en: The Pythagoreans stumbled on the fact that the square root of two cannot be expressed as a number. They invented ingenious ways of finding successive approximations for it. But, no matter how far the process is taken, you never get an exact answer. The result is always midway between two numbers. The further down the list you go, the closer you get to the value of the square root of two. But the process of successive approximation may be continued forever, without getting a precise result that can be expressed in a whole number.
body.review: 原文先写as a number，段末又写in a whole number，均照录。无理数的关键在于不能表示为两个整数之比，而不是不能表示为数或整数；“总在两数中间”也是底本表述。

zh: 因此，毕达哥拉斯学派不得不放弃“直线由有限个极小点组成”的观念，转而接受“直线由无限多个无维度的点组成”这一观点。巴门尼德则从另一个角度切入这一问题，主张直线是不可分割的。为了证明这一观点，芝诺试图揭示“无限可分”这一概念所导致的荒谬后果。此后数个世纪，数学家们都对“无限”这一概念避之唯恐不及。
en: The Pythagoreans thus had to abandon the idea of a line made up of a finite number of very small points, and accept that a line is made up of an infinite number of points with no dimension. Parmenides approached the issue from a different angle, arguing that a line was indivisible. In order to prove the point, Zeno tried to show the absurd consequences that would follow from the concept of infinite divisibility. For centuries after, mathematicians steered clear of the idea of infinity.

zh: 归根结底，所有这些悖论都源于连续统问题。所有试图通过数学定理（如收敛级数理论和集合论）来解决这些悖论的尝试，都只引发了新的矛盾。最终，芝诺的论点并未被推翻，因为它们基于一个真实的矛盾，而从形式逻辑的角度来看，这个矛盾是无法解答的。
en: Ultimately, all these paradoxes are derived from the problem of the continuum. All the attempts to resolve them by means of mathematical theorems, such as the theory of convergent series and the theory of sets have only given rise to new contradictions. In the end, Zeno’s arguments have not been refuted, because they are based on a real contradiction which, from the standpoint of formal logic, cannot be answered.

zh: 胡珀接着写道：
en: Hooper continues:

zh: 即使是戴德金（1831—1916）、康托尔（1845—1918）和罗素（1872—1970）为理清“数”的概念所引发的关于无限的悖论问题而提出的深奥论证，也最终导致了更多悖论的产生。
en: Even the abstruse arguments put forward by Dedekind (1831-1916), Cantor (1845-1918) and Russell (1872-1970) in their mighty efforts to straighten out the paradoxical problems of infinity into which we are led by our concept of ‘numbers,’ have resulted in the creation of still further paradoxes.

zh: 突破发生在十七、十八世纪，当时开普勒、卡瓦列里、帕斯卡、沃利斯、牛顿和莱布尼茨等人决定无视形式逻辑所提出的种种困难，转而处理无穷小量。其成果具有划时代的意义。如果不借助无穷的概念，整个现代数学——以及随之而来的物理学——都将无法运转。
en: The breakthrough came in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, when men like Kepler, Cavalieri, Pascal, Wallis, Newton and Leibniz decided to ignore the numerous difficulties raised by formal logic, and deal with infinitesimal quantities. The results were epoch-making. Without the use of infinity, the whole of modern mathematics, and with it physics, would be unable to function.

zh: 芝诺悖论所凸显的根本问题在于，形式逻辑无法把握运动。芝诺的“箭悖论”以飞行中的箭所描绘的抛物线为例说明运动。在这条轨迹的任何给定点上，箭都被视为静止的。但由于根据定义，一条直线由一系列点组成，而在每个点上箭都是静止的，因此运动不过是一种错觉。黑格尔给出了这一悖论的解答。
en: The essential problem, highlighted by Zeno’s paradoxes, is the inability of formal logic to grasp movement. Zeno’s Paradox of the Arrow takes as an example of movement the parabola traced by an arrow in flight. At any given point in this trajectory, the arrow is considered to be still. But since, by definition, a line consists of a series of points, at each of which the arrow is still, movement is an illusion. The answer to this paradox was given by Hegel.

zh: 运动的概念必然包含一种矛盾。试想一个物体（例如芝诺的箭）从一点移动到另一点的过程。当它开始运动时，它已不再位于点A。与此同时，它也尚未到达点B。那么，它究竟在哪里？若说它“在中间”，这种说法毫无意义，因为那样它仍处于某一点上，因此处于静止状态。“但是，”黑格尔说，“运动意味着既处于此处又不处于此处，从而同时处于两者之中；正是这种时空的连续性，才首先使运动成为可能。”
正如亚里士多德敏锐地指出的：“这源于人们理所当然地认为时间由‘当下’构成；因为如果不承认这一点，就无法得出相应的结论。”但这个“当下”究竟是什么？如果我们说箭在“这里”、“当下”，它就已经过去了。
en: The notion of movement necessarily involves a contradiction. Consider the movement of a body, Zeno’s arrow for example, from one point to another. When it starts to move, it is no longer at point A. At the same time, it is not yet at point B. Where is it, then? To say that it is ‘in the middle’ conveys nothing, for then it would still be at a point, and therefore at rest. “But,” says Hegel, “movement means to be in this place and not to be in it, and thus to be in both alike; this is the continuity of space and time which first makes motion possible.”

As Aristotle shrewdly observed, “It arises from the fact that it is taken for granted that time consists of the Now; for if this is not conceded, the conclusions will not follow.” But what is this ‘now’? If we say the arrow is ‘here’, ‘now’, it has already gone.

zh: 恩格斯写道：
en: Engels writes:

zh: 运动本身就是一种矛盾：即便是简单的机械性位置变化，也只能通过一个物体在同一时刻既位于一处又位于另一处、既位于同一位置又不在该位置来实现。而对这一矛盾的持续肯定与同时化解这一矛盾，正是运动的本质。
en: Motion itself is a contradiction: even simple mechanical change of place can only come about through a body being both in one place and in another place at one and the same moment of time, being in one and the same place and also not in it. And the continual assertion and simultaneous solution of this contradiction is precisely what motion is.

zh: 最早的原子论者
en: THE FIRST ATOMISTS

zh: 克拉佐梅纳的阿那克萨戈拉出生于公元前500 年左右，当时小亚细亚正处于与米底人的战争时期，雅典也在伯里克利领导下崛起。阿那克萨戈拉迁居雅典，与埃斯库罗斯、索福克勒斯、阿里斯托芬、第欧根尼和普罗泰戈拉是同时代人。他是一位远比他们更具原创性和思想深度的思想家，对雅典的哲学产生了巨大影响。亚里士多德曾说，他就像“醉汉中的清醒之人”。
阿那克萨戈拉秉承最优秀的爱奥尼亚传统，崇尚实验与观察。本杰明·法林顿指出：“毫无疑问，他将感官证据视为探究自然的不可或缺之物，但与恩培多克勒一样，他致力于证明存在一些过于微妙的物理过程，以至于我们的感官无法直接感知。”
en: Anaxagoras of Clazomenae was born around 500 BC, in Asia Minor, in the period of wars with the Medes, and the rise of Athens under Pericles. Anaxagoras moved to Athens, where he was a contemporary of Aeschylus, Sophocles, Aristophanes, Diogenes and Protagoras. He was a far more original and profound thinker, who had a tremendous impact on philosophy in Athens. Aristotle said that he was like “a sober man among drunkards”.

Anaxagoras, following the best Ionian tradition, believed in experiment and observation. “There can be no question,” says Benjamin Farrington, “but that he regarded sense-evidence as indispensable for the investigation of nature, but, like Empedocles, he was concerned to show that there were physical processes too subtle for our senses to perceive directly.”

zh: 他的科学发现堪称一流。他认为太阳是一团熔融的元素，恒星也是如此，尽管恒星距离太远，无法感受到它们的热量。月亮离我们更近，且由与地球相同的物质构成。月光是太阳光的反射，日食则是月亮遮挡太阳光所致。与后来的苏格拉底一样，他被指控为无神论者，这一指控可能属实，因为他在其宇宙论中几乎未提及宗教。这些革命性的思想震惊了保守的雅典人，最终导致阿那克萨戈拉被流放。
en: His scientific discoveries were of the first order. He believed that the sun was a mass of molten elements, as also were the stars, although these were too far away for their heat to be felt. The moon was nearer, and made of the same material as the earth. The light of the moon was a reflection of the sun, and eclipses were caused by the moon blocking off the sun’s light. Like Socrates later, he was accused of atheism, probably accurately, since he scarcely mentions religion in his cosmology. These revolutionary ideas shocked the conservative Athenians, eventually leading to Anaxagoras’ banishment.

zh: 与巴门尼德相反，阿那克萨戈拉认为万物皆可无限分割，甚至最微小的物质都包含着每种元素的成分。他还认为物质由多种粒子组成。因此，他提出疑问：面包被吃下后，为何会转化为骨骼、肌肉、血液、皮肤及其他组织？唯一的解释是，小麦粒子中必定以某种隐蔽的形式包含了构成身体所需的所有元素，这些元素在消化过程中被重新排列。
en: In opposition to Parmenides, Anaxagoras held that everything is infinitely divisible, and that even the smallest amount of matter contains some of each element. He also considered that matter was made up of particles of many kinds. Thus, he asked how it occurs that bread, when eaten, turns into bones, flesh, blood, skin, and the rest. The only explanation was that the particles of wheat must contain, in some hidden form, all the elements necessary for the makeup of the body, which are rearranged in the digestive process.

zh: 他认为存在无限多的元素或“种子”。但其中有一种元素扮演着特殊角色，那就是“努斯”（nous），通常被译为“心灵”。它比其他元素更轻，与其他元素不同，它未被混合，并作为一种组织和赋予生命的原则渗透于所有物质之中。正因如此，阿那克萨戈拉通常被视为唯心主义者。但这远非定论。作为彻底的唯心主义者的黑格尔认为，尽管“努斯”是迈向唯心主义的重要一步，“但在阿那克萨戈拉那里，这一思想尚未得到充分发展。”
阿那克萨戈拉的“努斯”也可以作唯物主义的解释，将其视为物质的内在驱动力，或者更准确地说，是能量。黑格尔本人也理解到，这并不意味着一种外部的智慧，而是发生在自然内部、赋予自然以形式和规定性的客观过程。
en: He believed there to be an infinite number of elements or ‘seeds’. But there was one of them which played a special role. This was the nous, usually translated as ‘mind’. Lighter than the other elements, it is, unlike the rest, unmixed, and permeates all matter, as an organising and animating principle. For this reason, Anaxagoras is usually regarded as an idealist. But this is far from certain. The arch-idealist Hegel considered that, while the nous was an important step in the direction of idealism, “with Anaxagoras it was not fully worked out.”

Anaxagoras’ nous can also have a materialistic interpretation, as the inner moving spirit of matter, or, more correctly expressed, energy. Hegel himself understood that it did not mean an external intelligence, but the objective processes which take place within nature, providing it with form and definition.

zh: 物质由无数肉眼不可见的微小粒子组成的观点，代表了一种极其重要的概括，也是向原子论的过渡——原子论是对现代科学的一次非凡预见，最早由留基伯（约公元前500—440 年）和德谟克利特（约公元前460—370 年）阐述。若考虑到这些思想家既没有电子显微镜，也没有任何其他技术辅助手段，这一突破就显得更加惊人。因此，当时既无办法证实该理论，更遑论进一步发展它。更重要的是，它招致了宗教界的愤怒，以及唯心主义者的蔑视，最终在中世纪漫长而黑暗的岁月里悄然湮没。直到后来，如同许多古代思想一样，它被文艺复兴时期的思想家（如伽森狄）重新发现，并在激发新的科学视野方面发挥了重要作用。
en: The idea that matter consists of an infinity of tiny particles, invisible to the senses, represents a most important generalisation, and a transition to the atomic theory, that remarkable anticipation of modern science, first expounded by Leucippus (c. 500-440 BC) and Democritus (c. 460-370 BC). The breakthrough was even more astonishing when we bear in mind that these thinkers had no access to electron microscopes, or any other technological aids. There was therefore no means of corroborating the theory, let alone developing it at that time. More importantly, it incurred the wrath of the religious, and the scorn of the idealists, and was allowed to sink without trace in the long, dark night of the Middle Ages. This was until, like so many ideas of antiquity, it was rediscovered by the thinkers of the Renaissance, like Gassendi, where it played an important role in stimulating the new scientific outlook.

zh: 关于留基伯，人们所知甚少，甚至有人怀疑他是否真实存在，不过赫库兰尼姆出土的纸草文书证实了他的存在。他的大部分言论是通过其他哲学家的著作流传至今的。留基伯提出了一个惊人地现代的假说：整个宇宙仅由两样东西构成，即原子和虚空（一种绝对真空）。他也是首位确立后来被称为“因果律”和“充足理由律”的哲学家。现存的唯一一段确凿的残篇写道：“没有任何事情是无缘无故发生的，一切皆有其依据且必然发生。”
早期原子论者是决定论者。他们将因果关系坚定地置于所有自然过程的核心，但采取的方式却十分僵化，令人联想到拉普拉斯后来的机械决定论。这种早期原子论者的僵化观点后来被伊壁鸠鲁所修正，他提出原子在虚空中下落时会发生轻微偏转，从而在必然性的框架中引入了偶然性这一要素。
en: About Leucippus, so little is known that some even doubted his existence, which, however, was proved by the discovery of papyri at Herculaneum. Most of his sayings have come down to us through the writings of other philosophers. In a startlingly modern hypothesis, Leucippus stated that the whole universe was made up of just two things, atoms and the void, an absolute vacuum. He was also the first to establish what later became known as the law of causality and the law of sufficient reason. The one authentic fragment which has survived says: “Naught happens for nothing, but everything from a ground and of necessity.”

The early atomists were determinists. They placed causality firmly at the centre of all natural processes, but they did so in an unbending way, reminiscent of the later mechanical determinism of Laplace. This rigidity of the earliest atomists was later corrected by Epicurus, who put forward the idea that atoms falling through the void swerve slightly, thus introducing the element of accident into the framework of necessity.

zh: 原子论者认为万物皆源于无数的基本粒子——原子（atoma，意为“不可分割之物”）。这些原子在性质上相同，但在量上不同，仅在大小、形状和重量上有所差异，尽管它们极其微小，以至于肉眼无法看见。从本质上讲，这一观点是正确的。整个物理世界，从煤炭到钻石，从人体到玫瑰的香气，都是由大小和重量各异的原子组成，并排列成分子。现代科学能够对这一论断给出精确的定量表述。古希腊原子论者却无力做到这一点，因为奴隶制生产方式固有的技术发展局限性，阻碍了当时那些卓越发明的合理利用——包括蒸汽机，这些发明大多仍停留在玩具和奇珍异物的层面。正因如此，他们能够预见二十世纪科学最重要的原理之一，就显得尤为了不起。
en: The atomists derived all things from an infinite number of fundamental particles, the atoma (which means ‘that which cannot be divided’). These atoms were alike in quality, but unlike in quantity, differing only in size, shape and weight, although the smallness of their size made it impossible to see them. In essence, this was correct. The entire physical world, from coal to diamonds, from the human body to the scent of roses, is composed of atoms of different sizes and weights, arranged in molecules. Present day science can give a precise quantitative expression to this assertion. The Greek atomists were in no position to do this, because the limitation upon the development of technology inherent in the slave method of production prevented the proper utilisation of the brilliant inventions of the time, including the steam engine, which mostly remained on the level of toys and curiosities. All the more remarkable, then, was the way in which they anticipated one of the most important principles of twentieth-century science.

zh: 著名美国物理学家理查德·P. 费曼强调了原子理论在当代科学中的地位：
en: The celebrated American physicist Richard P. Feynman underlines the place of atomic theory in present day science:

zh: 倘若因某种大灾难，所有的科学知识都被摧毁，而只能向后代生物传递一句话，那么哪句话能用最少的词语包含最多的信息？我相信那就是原子假说（或者说是原子事实，或者无论你愿意称它为什么）——万物皆由原子构成，这些微小的粒子永不停息地运动着，当它们相距不远时会相互吸引，但一旦被挤压在一起就会相互排斥。你会发现，只要稍加想象并进行思考，这一句话中就蕴含着关于世界的海量信息。
en: If, in some cataclysm, all of scientific knowledge were to be destroyed, and only one sentence passed onto the next generations of creatures, what statement would contain the most information in the fewest words? I believe it is the atomic hypothesis (or the atomic fact, or whatever you wish to call it) that all things are made of atoms – little particles that move around in perpetual motion, attracting each other when they are a little distance apart, but repelling upon being squeezed into one another. In that one sentence, you will see, there is an enormous amount of information about the world, if just a little imagination and thinking are applied.

zh: 他又说：
en: And again:

zh: 万物皆由原子构成。这是关键的假设。例如，在整个生物学领域中最重要的假设是：动物所做的一切，原子也能做到。换言之，生物所做的任何事情，都可以从“它们由遵循物理定律的原子构成”这一视角来理解。这一点并非一开始就为人所知：需要经过一些实验和理论推导才能提出这一假设，但如今它已被广泛接受，并且它也是在生物学领域产生新思想的最有用的理论。

如果一块钢或一块盐——它们由彼此紧邻的原子构成——都能具有如此有趣的特性；如果水——它不过是这些微小的液滴，在地球上绵延数英里、千篇一律——能够形成波浪和泡沫，并在流过水泥时发出湍急的声响并呈现奇特的图案；如果这一切，包括水流中的所有生命迹象，都不过是一堆原子，那么还有多少可能性是可能的呢？如果我们不再将原子排列成某种固定模式——那种不断重复、绵延不绝的模式，甚至不再形成像紫罗兰香气那样复杂的小团块——而是让原子在不同位置呈现出截然不同的排列，让不同种类的原子以多种方式组合，持续变化而不重复，那么这种“事物”的行为方式，又会有多么不可思议呢？难道在你面前来回走动、与你交谈的那个“东西”，可能是一团由这些原子以极其复杂的排列方式组成的巨大团块，其复杂程度之高，甚至让人难以想象它究竟能做什么？当我们说我们是一堆原子时，并非指我们仅仅是一堆原子，因为如果这堆原子的排列并非处处重复相同模式，那么它完全可能具备你在镜中看到的那些可能性。
en: Everything is made of atoms. That is the key hypothesis. The most important hypothesis in all of biology, for example, is that everything that animals do, atoms do. In other words, there is nothing that living things do that cannot be understood from the point of view that they are made of atoms acting according to the laws of physics. This was not known from the beginning: it took some experimenting and theorising to suggest this hypothesis, but now it is accepted, and it is the most useful theory for producing new ideas in the field of biology.

If a piece of steel or a piece of salt, consisting of atoms one next to the other, can have such interesting properties; if water – which is nothing but these little blobs, mile upon mile of the same thing over the earth – can form waves and foam, and make rushing noises and strange patterns as it runs over cement; if all of this, all the life of a stream of water, can be nothing but a pile of atoms, how much more is possible? If instead of arranging the atoms in some definite pattern, again and again repeated, on and on, or even forming little lumps of complexity like the odour of violets, we make an arrangement which is always different from place to place, with different kinds of atoms arranged in many ways, continually changing, not repeating, how much more marvellously is it possible that this thing might behave? Is it possible that that ‘thing’ walking back and forth in front of you, talking to you, is a great glob of these atoms in a very complex arrangement, such that the sheer complexity of it staggers the imagination as to what it can do? When we say we are a pile of atoms, we do not mean we are merely a pile of atoms, because a pile of atoms which is not repeated from one to the other might well have the possibilities which you see before you in the mirror.

zh: 古希腊原子论者的世界观自然是唯物主义的。这使他们招致了唯心主义者和宗教倾向者的憎恨。针对伊壁鸠鲁展开了一场尤为恶毒的诽谤运动，几个世纪以来，他的哲学观点被严重歪曲，以至于在大众的想象中变成了与其完全相反的内容。他们是自认的无神论者。在这种宇宙观中，没有上帝的容身之地。德谟克利特在原子本身的性质中发现了变异与变化的原因：原子在真空（“虚空”）中下落时相互碰撞，以不同方式排列组合，同类与同类结合。
en: The world outlook of the Greek atomists was naturally materialist. This earned them the hatred of the idealists and the religiously-inclined. A particularly spiteful campaign of calumny was directed against Epicurus, whose philosophical views were so distorted for centuries as to turn them into their exact opposite in the popular imagination. They were self-confessed atheists. There is no room for God in this view of the universe. Democritus found the cause of mutation and change in the nature of the atoms themselves: falling through the vacuum (the ‘void’), they impinge on one another, arranging themselves in different ways, like combining with like.

zh: 通过无穷无尽的各种组合，我们得到了自然界中随处可见的持续变化，这也导致了世间万物的无常。有无数个世界在“诞生与消亡”，它们并非由上帝创造，而是根据自然法则，出于必然性而产生并毁灭。对这些事物的认识主要源于感官知觉，但这只能让我们对自然有“模糊”的理解。必须通过“明晰”的理性来补充并超越这种认识，从而认知事物的本质——原子与虚空。科学唯物主义世界观的基本要素，都蕴含在这几行文字之中。
en: Through an endless series of different combinations, we get the constant changes which are everywhere to be seen in nature, and which give rise to the transitoriness of worldly things. There was an infinite number of worlds ‘born and dying’, not created by God, but arising and being destroyed out of necessity, in accordance with natural laws. Knowledge of these things is derived mainly from sensory perception, but this gives us only a ‘dim’ understanding of nature. It must be supplemented and transcended by ‘bright’ reason, which leads to the cognition of the essence of things, the atoms and the void. The fundamental elements of a scientific materialist world outlook are all present in these few lines.

zh: 德谟克利特的哲学思想由伊壁鸠鲁进一步发展和深化。与他的导师一样，他明确否认神明对世间事务的干预，其理论基础是物质的永恒性及其持续运动的状态。然而，他拒绝了留基伯和德谟克利特的机械决定论，提出了原子会自发地（受内部条件制约）“偏离”其运行轨道的观点，以此解释在真空空间中以相同速度运动的原子之间发生碰撞的可能性。这是向前迈出的重要一步，提出了必然性与偶然性之间的辩证关系——这是现代物理学至今仍在苦苦思索的关键理论问题之一，尽管黑格尔早已找到了答案。
en: The philosophy of Democritus was further developed and deepened by Epicurus. Like his mentor, he explicitly denied the interference of the gods in the affairs of the world, basing himself on the eternity of matter, in a state of continual motion. However, he rejected the mechanistic determinism of Leucippus and Democritus, introducing the idea of a spontaneous (internally conditioned) ‘deviation’ of the atoms from their course, in order to explain the possibility of collisions between atoms moving at equal speed through empty space. This was an important step forward, posing the dialectical relation between necessity and chance – one of the key theoretical questions over which modern physics is still wracking its brains, although the solution was found long ago by Hegel.

zh: 伊壁鸠鲁的认识论完全基于对感官所提供信息的接受。“所有感官都是真实的传报者”，
也没有任何东西能够反驳感官。在此，他的论述虽然基于一个正确的假设——我通过感官来解读世界——但相对于德谟克利特而言，这却是一种倒退。这种观点过于片面。感官知觉无疑是所有知识的基础，但必须懂得如何正确解读感官信息。这就是赫拉克利特所说的：“如果人的灵魂无法理解感官的语言，那么眼睛和耳朵对人来说就是糟糕的见证者。”
狭隘的经验主义方法必然导致错误。因此，据西塞罗所述，德谟克利特认为太阳巨大无比，而伊壁鸠鲁则认为其直径仅约两英尺。然而，在其他方面，伊壁鸠鲁却做了一些惊人的发现。伽森狄——他可被视为现代原子论之父——曾盛赞伊壁鸠鲁，因为后者仅凭推理就揭示了后来通过实验证实的事实：所有物体，无论其质量和重量如何，从高处向下坠落时都具有相同的速度。
en: Epicurus’ theory of knowledge is based entirely on acceptance of the information given to us by the senses. “All senses are heralds of the true”,

nor is there anything that can refute the senses. Here his presentation, while starting from a correct assumption – I interpret the world through my senses – represents a step back in relation to Democritus. It is too one-sided. Sense perception is undoubtedly the basis of all knowledge, but it is necessary to know how to interpret correctly the information of the senses. That is what Heraclitus meant when he said that: “Eyes and ears are bad witnesses to men if they have souls that understand not their language.”

The narrow empirical approach invariably leads to errors. Thus, according to Cicero, Democritus thought that the sun was immensely large, whereas Epicurus believed it to be only about two feet in diameter. In other respects, however, Epicurus made some startling discoveries. Gassendi, who may be considered the father of modern atomism, praised Epicurus because, exclusively by reasoning, he showed the fact later demonstrated by experiment, that all bodies, irrespective of their mass and weight, have the same velocity when falling from above to below.

zh: 卢克莱修论宗教
en: LUCRETIUS ON RELIGION

zh: 伊壁鸠鲁及其追随者向那种以人们的恐惧和无知为生计的宗教宣战。卢克莱修那部伟大的哲学诗作《论宇宙的本质》的第一卷，实质上是一份唯物主义和无神论的宣言：
en: Epicurus and his followers declared war upon religion which feeds off men’s fear and ignorance. The first book of Lucretius’ great philosophical poem On The Nature of the Universe contains what amounts to a materialist and atheist manifesto:

zh: 当人类的生命在众目之下卑微地匍匐，被迷信的沉重枷锁压倒在地——那迷信的狰狞面孔从天空四面八方阴森地俯视着凡人——一位希腊人率先昂起凡人的目光予以反抗，率先挺直身躯勇敢地迎接挑战。诸神的传说未能将他击垮，闪电的劈啪与天穹的咆哮威胁亦未能使他屈服。相反，这些反而激发了他的男子气概，使他成为人类中第一个渴望击碎自然之门上束缚锁链的人。他心灵中蓬勃的生命力最终占了上风。他大胆地越过世界燃烧的城墙，在思想中穿越了无限的宇宙。凯旋而归后，他向我们宣告了何为可能、何为不可能：万物之力皆有定界，皆有不可动摇的边界。因此，迷信反倒被他踩在脚下，而我们因他的胜利，得以升至与天空齐平。
en: When human life lay grovelling in all men’s sight, crushed to the earth under the dead weight of superstition whose grim features loured menacingly upon mortals from the four quarters of the sky, a man of Greece was first to raise mortal eyes in defiance, first to stand erect and brave the challenge. Fables of the gods did not crush him, nor the lightning flash and the growling menace of the sky. Rather, they quickened his manhood, so that he, first of all men, longed to smash the constraining locks of nature’s doors. The vital vigour of his mind prevailed. He ventured far out beyond the flaming ramparts of the world and voyaged in mind throughout infinity. Returning victorious, he proclaimed to us what can be and what cannot: how a limit is fixed to the power of everything and an immovable frontier post. Therefore superstition in its turn lies crushed beneath his feet, and we by his triumph are lifted level with the skies.

zh: 即便在此处，译者的宗教偏见也显而易见。他始终不愿将“religio”一词译为“宗教”，而宁愿将其译作“迷信”。这可是1951 年的事！伊壁鸠鲁的唯物主义哲学对年轻的卡尔·马克思产生了巨大影响，他在大学期间便选择以此作为博士论文的主题。马克思认为，罗马哲学家兼诗人卢克莱修是“古人中唯一真正理解伊壁鸠鲁物理学的人”，他写下了“更深刻的阐述”。
en: Even here, the religious prejudices of the translator are apparent. He cannot bring himself to translate the word religio as religion, preferring to render it as ‘superstition’. This, in 1951! The materialist philosophy of Epicurus made a big impact on the young Karl Marx, who chose it as the subject of his doctoral dissertation while at university. Marx considered that the Roman philosopher-poet Lucretius was “the only one in general of all the ancients who has understood Epicurean physics”, who has written “a more profound exposition”.

zh: 卢克莱修以极富感染力的诗意语言，捍卫了物质不可毁灭的观点——即物质既不能被创造，也不能被毁灭这一正确理念：
en: In the most striking poetic language, Lucretius defends the indestructibility of matter, the correct idea that matter can neither be created nor destroyed:

zh: 这种心灵的恐惧与黑暗，无法被阳光——那些白昼中闪耀的光束——驱散，而只能通过理解自然的外部形态和内在运作机制来消除。在探讨这一主题时，我们的出发点将是这一原则：神圣的力量绝不可能无中生有。所有凡人之所以如此深陷恐惧，是因为他们看到天地间发生种种现象却找不到明显的原因，于是便将这些归因于神的意志。因此，当我们认识到“无中生有”绝无可能时，便能更清晰地看清前方的道路，即在没有诸神协助的情况下，万物如何被创造并产生的问题。
en: This dread and darkness of the mind cannot be dispelled by the sunbeams, the shining shafts of day, but only by an understanding of the outward form and inner workings of nature. In tackling this theme, our starting-point will be this principle: Nothing can ever be created by divine power out of nothing. The reason why all mortals are so gripped by fear is that they see all sorts of things happening on the earth and in the sky with no discernible cause, and these they attribute to the will of a god. Accordingly, when we have seen that nothing can be created out of nothing, we shall then have a clearer picture of the path ahead, the problem of how things are created and occasioned without the aid of the gods.

zh: 十九世纪中叶，迈耶、焦耳、赫尔姆霍兹等人证实的能量守恒定律表明，当能量从一种形式转化为另一种形式时，其总量既不会消失，也不会凭空产生。这为“物质既不能被创造，也不能被毁灭”这一唯物主义立场提供了坚不可摧的基础。卢克莱修也精彩地阐述了这一思想：
en: The law of the conservation of energy, proved by Mayer, Joule, Helmholz and others in the mid-nineteenth century shows that the total amount of energy neither disappears nor is created, when changing from one kind to another. This provides an unshakeable basis for the materialist position that matter can neither be created nor destroyed. This idea is also brilliantly conveyed by Lucretius:

zh: 第二个伟大原理是：自然将万物分解为构成它们的原子，但绝不会使任何事物归于虚无。如果万物的各个部分都是易朽的，那么任何事物都可能突然消亡并从视野中消失。届时便无需任何力量来分离其各部分并松动它们的联系。事实上，由于万物皆由不可毁灭的种子构成，自然显然不会允许任何事物消亡，除非它遭遇了一种力量——这种力量要么一击将其击碎，要么潜入缝隙中，将它拆解开来。
en: The second great principle is this: nature resolves everything into its component atoms and never reduces anything to nothing. If anything were perishable in all its parts, anything might perish all of a sudden and vanish from sight. There would be no need of any force to separate its parts and loosen their links. In actual fact, since everything is composed of indestructible seeds, nature obviously does not allow anything to perish till it has encountered a force that shatters it with a blow or creeps into chinks and unknits it.

zh: 伊壁鸠鲁的世界观认为，宇宙是无限的，物质无论在外部还是内部都无边无际：
en: The Epicurean world view maintains that the universe is infinite, and matter has no limit, either externally or internally:

zh: 如果不存在这样的最小部分，那么即使是最小的物体也将由无限多的部分组成，因为它们总能被一分为二，而其每一半又可以无限次地继续一分为二。依此推论，整个宇宙与最微小的物体之间会有什么区别呢？根本没有。因为，无论宇宙多么无穷无尽，最微小的物体同样由无限多的部分组成。
en: If there are no such least parts, even the smallest bodies will consist of an infinite number of parts, since they can always be halved and their halves halved again without limit. On this showing, what difference will there be between the whole universe and the very least of things? None at all. For, however endlessly infinite the universe may be, yet the smallest things will equally consist of an infinite number of parts.

zh: 而且：
en: And:

zh: 因此，请明白：宇宙在任何方向上都是无边界的。倘若它有边界，就必然在某处存在一个极限。但显然，除非有外部之物加以限制，否则事物不可能有极限——这样，视线才能追随它到某一点，却无法越过该点。既然你必须承认宇宙之外一无所有，那么宇宙就不可能有极限，因而也是无尽的、无法衡量的。
en: Learn, therefore, that the universe is not bounded in any direction. If it were, it would necessarily have a limit somewhere. But clearly a thing cannot have a limit unless there is something outside to limit it, so that the eye can follow it up to a certain point but not beyond. Since you must admit that there is nothing outside the universe, it can have no limit and is accordingly without end or measure.

zh: 如果我们这个时代的科学家能拥有同样扎实的哲学视野，我们本可以避免那些最显而易见的方法论错误，例如寻找“物质的基元”、主张有限宇宙的“大爆炸”理论、“时间的诞生”，以及同样荒谬的“物质的持续创造”等观点。关于时间，德谟克利特指出，时间没有起源，它本身并不独立存在，而是依附于事物的运动或静止状态。这比某些当今物理学家所宣称的二百亿年前所谓的“时间的开端”要科学得多！在仪器设备方面，他们固然更先进，但在思维方式上，却远远落后于早期的唯物主义者。
en: If the scientists of our own era had had an equally sound philosophical outlook, we would have been spared the most glaring errors of method, such as the search for the ‘bricks of matter’, the ‘big bang’ with its finite universe, the ‘birth of time’, the equally absurd ‘continuous creation of matter’, and the like. In relation to time, Democritus stated that time had no origin, that it does not exist in itself, apart from the movement of things or things at rest. How infinitely more scientific than certain present-day physicists who talk about the alleged ‘beginning of time’ twenty billion years ago! In their apparatus, they are more advanced, but in their mode of thinking, they are worlds behind the early materialists.
body.review: 二百亿年对应底本twenty billion；此处宇宙论评价和年代均为作者原文的论断，按底本保留。

zh: 伊壁鸠鲁一贯的唯物主义世界观，使他自古以来就遭受了教会最恶毒的攻击。使徒保罗在《使徒行传》中专门提到了他们。
在但丁的时代，被指控为伊壁鸠鲁主义者，意味着此人否认圣灵和灵魂的不朽。总体而言，人们认为伊壁鸠鲁倡导一种无道德的享乐主义哲学，其中各种暴食和放荡行为皆被容许。这一切不过是对伊壁鸠鲁及其哲学的粗鄙诽谤。
en: The consistent materialist outlook of Epicurus earned him the most venomous attacks of the Church from the earliest times. The apostle Paul specifically mentions them in the Acts of the Apostles.

In Dante’s time, the accusation of Epicureanism meant someone who denied the Holy Ghost and the immortality of the soul. In general, Epicurus is thought to have advocated an amoral and hedonistic philosophy, in which all manner of gluttony and licentiousness was permitted. All this is just a crude slander against Epicurus and his philosophy.

zh: 就道德和伦理而言，伊壁鸠鲁哲学代表了人类精神最崇高的产物之一。它与斯宾诺莎的那句名言如出一辙：“既不哭泣，也不欢笑，而是理解。”伊壁鸠鲁致力于通过对自然及其间人类地位的清晰理解，使人类摆脱恐惧。他自问：一切恐惧的根源是什么？并回答道：是对死亡的恐惧。他的主要目标是消除这种恐惧，他解释道：死亡对我而言，在当下毫无意义，因为我尚在人世；在将来也与我无关，因为死后，我将对此一无所知。因此，他敦促人们抛开对死亡的恐惧，充分地生活。这种美好而人道的哲学，一直被那些企图将人们的目光从现实世界的问题上转移到所谓“死后世界”的人所唾弃——据称那个世界会根据我们的所作所为给予奖赏或惩罚。
en: In terms of morality and ethics, the Epicurean philosophy represents one of the noblest products of the human spirit. It resembles the famous dictum of Spinoza: Neither weep nor laugh, but understand. Epicurus sought to free humanity from fear by promoting a clear understanding of nature and man’s place in it. He asked himself what is the basis of all fear, and answered, the fear of death. His main aim was to eliminate this fear, by explaining that death is nothing for me in the present, for I am alive, and will be nothing to me in the future, since, after death, I can know nothing about it. Therefore, he urged men to set aside fear of death and live life to the full. This beautiful and humane philosophy has always been anathema to those who wish to direct the eyes of men and women away from the problems of the real world to an alleged world after death, which is supposed to reward or punish us according to our just deserts.

zh: 针对伊壁鸠鲁的“粗俗”和“享乐主义”指控，源于基督教护教者对一种乐观且颂扬生命的哲学所持的报复性态度——这种哲学与他们的立场截然相反。他们企图用一堆诽谤将对手埋葬。事实上，伊壁鸠鲁与斯宾诺莎一样，将“善”等同于快乐，或无痛苦的状态。他从效用的角度审视人际关系，而友谊正是这种观点的最高体现。在社会动荡不安、充满不确定性的时期，他倡导超脱尘世，过一种宁静冥想的生活。他建议人们将需求降至最低，远离充满纷争、竞争和战争的世界。这当然是一种乌托邦式的想法，但与唯物主义的反对者们散布的丑陋而恶毒的讽刺形象毫无关系。伊壁鸠鲁直至临终仍坚守自己的理想，他在病榻上写道：
en: The accusation of grossness and hedonism against Epicurus stems from the vengeful attitude of the Christian apologists against a cheerful and life-enhancing philosophy – the exact opposite of their own. They sought to bury their enemy under a heap of slander. In fact, Epicurus, like Spinoza, identified the good with pleasure, or the absence of pain. He considered human relations from the point of view of utility, which finds its highest expression in friendship. In a period of great social turbulence and uncertainty, he preached withdrawal from the world, and a life of peaceful meditation. He recommended men to reduce their needs to a minimum, away from the world of strife, competition and war. This was, of course, a utopian idea, but it is nothing to do with the ugly and spiteful caricature put in circulation by the opponents of materialism. Epicurus remained true to his ideals on his deathbed, from where he wrote:

zh: 今天是我写信给你们的幸福日子……我所感受到的痛苦……已无法更甚。但这一切都被灵魂所体验的幸福所抵消，因为它忆起了我们过去的谈话。
en: A happy day is this on which I write to you … The pains which I feel … could not be greater. But all of this is opposed by the happiness which the soul experiences, remembering our conversations of a bygone time.

zh: 唯心主义的兴起
en: THE RISE OF IDEALISM

zh: “辩证法”一词源自希腊语“dialektike”，由“dialegomai”（交谈或讨论）衍生而来。最初，它指代辩论的艺术，其最高形式可见于柏拉图的《苏格拉底对话录》。这绝非偶然，而是源于雅典民主制度的本质——在公民大会上，演说与辩论拥有广阔的空间。这催生了一批新型公众人物、职业教师及各类演说家，从勇敢的自由思想家和深邃的哲学家，到不择手段的煽动家，不一而足。
en: The term ‘dialectics’ comes from the Greek ‘dialektike’, derived from ‘dialegomai’, to converse, or discuss. Originally, it signified the art of discussion, which may be seen in its highest form in the Socratic dialogues of Plato. This was no accident, but flowed from the very nature of Athenian democracy, with its ample scope for oratory and debate in public assemblies. This gave rise to a new breed of public figures, professional teachers and speakers of all kinds, from courageous freethinkers and profound philosophers to unscrupulous demagogues.

zh: 在现代人听来，“诡辩家”和“诡辩”这两个词听起来极不光彩，暗示着以巧妙的措辞掩盖的思想上的不诚实、诡计和谎言。事实上，诡辩最终确实沦落至此。但情况并非一直如此。从某种意义上说，他们可以与十八世纪法国启蒙运动的哲学家相提并论。他们是理性主义者和自由思想家，反对一切现有的教条和正统观念。他们的信条是“对一切持怀疑态度”。所有现存的事物和思想都必须接受最彻底的批判。这无疑蕴含着革命性和辩证法的内核。
en: To modern ears, the words ‘sophist’ and ‘sophistry’ have a thoroughly disreputable ring about them, suggesting intellectual dishonesty, trickery and lies, masked by clever turns of phrase. That, indeed, was how sophism ended up. But it was not always so. In a way, they can be compared to the philosophers of the French Enlightenment in the eighteenth century. They were rationalists and freethinkers, who stood opposed to all existing dogmas and orthodoxy. Their maxim was ‘Doubt Everything’. All existing things and ideas had to be subjected to the most far-reaching criticism. This undoubtedly contained a revolutionary and dialectical kernel.

zh: 施韦格勒写道：
en: Schwegler writes:

zh: 在这一新开拓的领域里，智者们如今尽情嬉戏，以少年般的热情享受着行使主体性的力量的乐趣，并通过主观辩证法，摧毁了一切曾经被客观确立的东西。
en: On this new-won field now the Sophists disported, enjoying with boyish exuberance the exercise of the power of subjectivity, and destroying, by means of a subjective dialectic, all that had been ever objectively established.

zh: 智者学派的活动反映了雅典与斯巴达之间伯罗奔尼撒战争时期的雅典生活。他们既是学者，也是实干家，是首批收取教学费用的教师。柏拉图在《理想国》中指出，智者学派的教义所表达的，不过是指导大众在公民和社会关系中行为的那些原则罢了。政界人士对他们的迫害之深，恰恰证明了这些政界人士对智者的嫉妒之深。智者们之所以遭到攻击，是因为他们主张道德和真理是主观概念，任何人都可以根据自己的个人偏好和利益来加以界定。但他们只不过是道出了实践中早已确立的规范罢了。今天我们也能看到同样的情况。职业政客们并不喜欢被人提醒那些在权力走廊中真正起作用的道德准则！
en: The activities of the sophists reflected life in Athens during the period of the Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta. They were both scholars and practical men, the first ones to charge a fee for teaching. Plato remarks in the Republic that the doctrines of the Sophists express only the same principles which guided the practice of the multitude in their civil and social relations. The hate with which they were persecuted by the statesmen proves the jealousy with which the latter saw them. The sophists were attacked for saying that morality and truth were subjective concepts, which could be determined by anyone, according to his personal preferences and interests. But they were only saying what was already the established norm in practice. We see the same thing today. Professional politicians do not like to be reminded of the moral code which really operates in the corridors of power!

zh: 施韦格勒继续写道：
en: Schwegler continues:

zh: 公共生活已沦为激情与私欲的角斗场；伯罗奔尼撒战争期间动荡雅典的党派纷争，已使道德情操变得迟钝并遭到扼杀；每个人都习惯于将个人私利置于国家利益和公共福祉之上，并以自身的意志和利益作为行动的标准与指导原则。普罗泰戈拉那句“人是万物的尺度”的格言，在实践中被奉行得再真实不过；而修辞学在公众集会和决策中的影响力，民众及其领袖的腐败，以及贪婪、虚荣以及党派之风所暴露的弱点，都为这种行为提供了太多施展的机会。那些既定并沿袭至今的规范已丧失权威，政治法规被视为任意的限制，道德原则被视为精心策划的政治训练的结果，对神明的信仰被视为人类为威慑自由活动而发明的东西，虔诚则被视为源于人类的法规，每个人都有权通过说服的艺术来改变它。将自然与理性的必然性与普遍性降格为纯粹人为规定的偶然性，这正是智者学派与当时有教养阶层普遍意识产生共鸣的关键所在；且无法断定其中理论与实践各占多少比重；究竟是智者们仅仅仅把现实生活表述为理论公式，还是社会腐败更多是源于智者们对其同时代人整个思想领域所施加的破坏性影响。
en: Public life was become an arena of passion and self-seeking; the party-strifes, which agitated Athens during the Peloponnesian war, had blunted and stifled the moral sentiment; every one accustomed himself to set his own private interest above that of the state and of the common good, and to seek in his own self-will and his own advantage the standard of his action and the principle of his guidance. The axiom of Protagoras, man is the measure of all things, was in practice only all too truly followed, while the influence of rhetoric in public assemblies and decisions, the corruption of the masses and their leaders, the weak points which cupidity, vanity, and party-spirit betrayed to the crafty, offered only all too much occasion for its exercise. What was established, and had come down so, had lost its authority, political regulation appeared as arbitrary restriction, moral principle as a result of calculated political training, faith in the gods as human invention for the intimidation of free activity, piety as a statute of human origin which every man had a right to alter by the art of persuasion. This reduction of the necessity and universality of nature and reason to the contingency of mere human appointment, is mainly the point where the Sophists are in contact with the general consciousness of the cultivated classes of the time; and it is impossible to decide what share theory had here, and what practice; whether the Sophists only found practical life in a theoretical formula, or whether the social corruption was rather a consequence of the destructive influence which the Sophists exercised over the entire circle of the opinions of their contemporaries.

zh: 那个动荡的时代——伴随着不断的变迁、战争、破坏与不安——在辩证矛盾的躁动精神中得到了映射。这种颠覆既有观念、令人不安的思想运动，恰恰反映了伯罗奔尼撒战争时期希腊的实际状况。同样，为了通过巧妙的论辩在民众大会或法庭上赢得支持，这一需求为一代职业演说家和辩证学家的崛起提供了物质基础。但这并不意味着智者学说的最初内容是由个人利益或金钱利益的考量所决定的，正如加尔文主义并非如此一样。然而，鉴于当时盛行的社会条件，智者学说后来的发展早已注定。
en: The turbulence of the times, with constant changes, wars, destruction and unrest, found a reflection in the restless spirit of dialectical contradiction. The unsettling movement of thought, upsetting existing ideas, mirrored the actual conditions of Greece at the time of the Peloponnesian wars. Likewise, the need to win over the assembly or law-court by clever argument provided a material base for the rise of a generation of professional orators and dialecticians. But that is not to say that the initial content of sophism was determined by considerations of personal advantage or pecuniary gain, any more than was, say, Calvinism. But, given the prevailing social conditions, the later development of sophism was determined in advance.

zh: 第一代智者是真正的哲学家，他们往往与民主政治以及对自然的唯物主义理解联系在一起。他们是理性主义者和通才，正如1789 年前几十年里的法国同行一样。同样地，他们机智过人，能够从问题的各个方面进行论证。普罗泰戈拉以道德导师著称，高尔吉亚以修辞家和政治家闻名，普罗迪库斯以语法学家和词源学家著称，希皮亚斯则被视为博学者。他们在各行各业和知识领域中均有身手。但这一运动——其实从未真正形成一个学派——逐渐开始走向堕落。那些四处游走、为谋取高薪和富有的赞助人而从一个城镇到另一个城镇的“智者”，逐渐成了令人鄙视和嘲笑的对象。
en: The first generation of sophists were genuine philosophers, often identified with democratic politics and with a materialist understanding of nature. They were rationalists and encyclopaedists, just as their French equivalents in the decades before 1789. And in the same way, they were clever and witty, with an ability to deal with all sides of a problem. Protagoras was celebrated as a teacher of morals, Gorgias as a rhetorician and politician, Prodicus as a grammarian and etymologist, and Hippias as a polymath. They were to be found in all the professions and spheres of knowledge. But gradually the movement, which really never constituted a real school, began to degenerate. The wandering ‘wise man’ going from town to town in search of good pay and a rich patron became a figure of contempt and ridicule.

zh: 本文所探讨的所有先前思想学派的共同特征在于其客观性，即认为我们的观念是否有效，取决于它们与客观现实——即我们身外的世界——的契合程度。智者们完全背离了这一点，转而主张哲学上的主观性。普罗泰戈拉（公元前481—411 年）那句著名的格言很好地概括了这一点：“人是万物的尺度；有的，就是有的；没有的，就是没有的。”
en: The common feature of all the previous schools of thought examined here is their objectivity, the assumption that the validity of our ideas depends on the degree to which they correspond to objective reality, to the world outside us. The sophists broke entirely from this, advancing instead the position of philosophical subjectivity. This is well summed up in the celebrated phrase of Protagoras (481-411 BC), “Man is the measure of all things; of that which is, that is; of that which is not, that is not.

zh: 关于这句话的确切含义存在一些争议，它也可以被解释为普罗泰戈拉是一位唯物主义者——这一观点与塞克斯图斯·恩皮里科斯的一段评论相吻合，即普罗泰戈拉曾指出万物的主要原因（“逻各斯”）在于物质。但毫无疑问，智者学说的大体趋势是朝着极端主观主义的方向发展的。由于他们对现有信仰和偏见进行了猛烈抨击，因此在保守派圈子里被视为颠覆分子。普罗泰戈拉本人因无神论而被驱逐出雅典，他的著作《论诸神》也被焚毁。
en: There is some dispute about the exact meaning of this phrase, which may also be put in a way which implies that Protagoras was a materialist, a view which fits in with a remark of Sextus Empiricus, to the effect that Protagoras said that the main causes (‘logoses’) of all things are in matter. But there can be no doubt that the general trend of sophism was in the direction of extreme subjectivism. As a result of their withering attacks on existing beliefs and prejudices, they were regarded as subversives in conservative circles. Protagoras himself was expelled from Athens for atheism, and his book On the Gods was burnt.

zh: 宗教信仰及其哲学对应物——教条主义——并非文化。就连赫拉克利特，尽管智慧非凡，也未能摆脱教条主义和狭隘的思维定式，这从他言论的语气中便可看出。但沿着这条道路，不可能取得真正的进步。因此，智者学说——至少在其早期阶段——在将旧有的普遍教条分解为各个组成部分，并使各部分相互对立方面，发挥了积极的作用。其消极一面在于，这些孤立的要素容易被以典型的“诡辩家”方式曲解并脱离语境。然而，正如黑格尔所言：“一个有教养的人……懂得对任何事物都说出一番道理，在一切事物中找到不同的视角。”
事实上，黑格尔认为，在柏拉图同名对话录中，普罗泰戈拉的论点优于苏格拉底的论点。
en: Religious conviction and its philosophical counterpart, dogmatism, is not culture. Even Heraclitus, despite his great wisdom, was not free from a dogmatic and narrow cast of mind, as shown by the tone of his utterances. But no real progress is possible along this path. Sophism, therefore, at least in its first period, played a positive role in breaking down the old universal dogmas into their component parts and counterposing each of the parts to the others. There was a negative side, in that the isolated elements were open to be twisted and turned out of context, in a typically ‘sophist’ way. Yet, as Hegel says: “A man of culture … knows how to say something of everything, to find points of view in all.”
In fact, Hegel thought that the arguments of Protagoras in Plato’s dialogue of that name were superior to those of Socrates.

zh: 这种“机智”（esprit）与盎格鲁-撒克逊的传统和思维方式完全格格不入，后者通常对此怀有难以掩饰的怀疑和厌恶。然而，正如黑格尔所深刻指出的，智者学说标志着现代意义上文化的开端。因为文化预设了对事物的理性考量和选择。
en: This kind of esprit (wit) is entirely foreign to the Anglo-Saxon tradition and mentality, which generally regards it with ill-concealed suspicion, and distaste. Yet, as Hegel, penetratingly observes, sophism marks the beginning of culture in the modern sense of the word. For culture presupposes a rational consideration of things and a choice.

zh: 事实上，一个有教养的人或一个有教养的民族最引人注目之处，在于其善于言辞的艺术，或者说善于从多角度审视和探讨问题。未受教养的人会觉得，与那些能轻松把握并表达各种观点的人交往令人不快。从这个意义上说，法国人是优秀的演说家，而德国人却称他们的谈话为“闲聊”；但带来这种效果的并非单纯的谈论，因为这还需要教养。我们或许已完全掌握了一篇演讲，但若缺乏教养，那便算不上是好的演讲。因此，人们学习法语，不仅是为了能说好法语，更是为了获得法兰西文化。因此，从智者那里所能获得的，正是将多种视角时刻铭记于心的能力，从而使审视某物时所能运用的丰富范畴，能立即浮现在脑海中。
en: In fact, what is most striking in a man or people of culture is the art of speaking well, or of turning subjects round and considering them in many aspects. The uncultivated man finds it unpleasant to associate with people who know how to grasp and express every point of view with ease. The French are good speakers in this sense, and the Germans call their talking prattle; but it is not mere talk that brings about this result, for culture is also wanted. We may have mastered a speech quite completely, but if we have not culture, it is not good speaking. Men thus learn French, not only to be able to speak French well, but to acquire French culture. What is to be obtained from the Sophists is thus the power of keeping the manifold points of view present to the mind, so that the wealth of categories by which an object may be considered, immediately occurs to it.

zh: 尽管诡辩术在当今社会声名狼藉，但它却是现代职业政治、法律和外交的真正鼻祖。我们以令人厌倦的规律性观察到，资产阶级政客们总是准备好以看似完全确信的态度，时而捍卫一种立场，时而又捍卫与其截然相反的立场，无论哪种情况，他们都会援引最令人信服的道德和实际论据。同样的套路在法庭上每天都能看到。何必再向读者罗列世界各国政府外交使团所施行的那些炉火纯青的谎言、诡计与欺骗的例子呢？这些人兼具诡辩家的一切缺点，却毫无其美德！
en: Despite the disrepute in which sophism is supposed to be held nowadays, it is the true father of modern professional politics, law and diplomacy. We observe with tedious regularity how bourgeois politicians are prepared to defend with apparently total conviction, now one position, now precisely the opposite, adducing in either case the most impressive moral and practical arguments. The same procedure may be observed in the law courts any day of the week. And why bother the reader with a list of examples of the consummate lying, manoeuvring deceit practised by the diplomatic corps of every government in the world? These people have all the faults of the sophists and none of their virtues!

zh: 诚然，智者们靠着敏捷的头脑和几乎能为任何事情辩护或反驳的能力谋生，就像律师代表辩方或控方进行论辩一样，而不顾案件本身的对错（动词“sophizesthai”意为“靠聪明谋生”）。他们是精明律师和职业政客的原型。但他们远不止于此。即便在智者那些在道德上更值得商榷的行为中，也蕴含着真正的哲学原则。正如黑格尔机智地指出的：
en: It is true that the sophists made a living out of their nimble wits and ability to argue for or against almost anything, as a lawyer argues for the defence or the prosecution, irrespective of the intrinsic rights and wrongs of the case (the verb ‘sophizesthai’ meant ‘making a career by being clever’). They were the prototype of the smart lawyer and the professional politician. But they were much more than that. Even in the more morally questionable activities of the sophists, there was a real philosophical principle involved. As Hegel wittily observes:

zh: “在最恶劣的行为中，也存在一种本质上真实的观点；如果将这一点凸显出来，人们就会为该行为开脱并加以辩护……”一个人无需在学识上取得多大进步，就能为最糟糕的行为准备好正当理由；自亚当时代以来，世间发生的一切，都曾被某种正当理由所辩护。
en: In the worst action there exists a point of view which is essentially real; if this is brought to the front, men excuse and vindicate the action… A man does not require to make great progress in his education to have good reasons ready for the worst action; all that has happened in the world since the time of Adam has been justified by some good reason.

zh: 智者派辩证法背后的基本思想是：真理是多方面的。这是一个极其重要的真理，也是整个辩证法的基础。区别在于它的运用方式。科学、客观的辩证法力求全面地把握每一个现象。主观辩证法，即智者派的辩证法，则从整体中选取某一方面，并将其与其他方面对立起来。通过这种方式，便有可能通过坚持某一部分——该部分本身完全合理——来否定整体。这是法律骗子、折中主义者的方法，也是“常识”以一种更粗糙的方式所采用的方法，即基于个别现象作出武断的假设。
en: The basic idea which underlies the dialectic of sophism is that truth is many-sided. This is an extremely important truth, and fundamental to the dialectical method in general. The difference lies in the use to which it is put. Scientific, objective dialectics strives to grasp every phenomenon in an all-round manner. Subjective dialectics, the dialectic of sophism, takes one or another aspect of the whole, and counterposes it to the rest. In this way, it is possible to deny the whole by insisting on the part, which, in itself, is perfectly sound. This is the method of the legal charlatan, the eclectic, and also, in a cruder way, of ‘common sense’, which makes arbitrary assumptions based upon particulars.

zh: 他们试图利用芝诺和赫拉克利特的论点来为其观点辩护，但采取的却是一种消极且片面的方式。例如，赫拉克利特曾说，人不可能两次踏入同一条河流。他的一个弟子更进一步，声称人甚至无法踏入同一条河流一次！然而，这是错误的。赫拉克利特的思想是：万物既存在又不存在，因为万物都在流变之中，不断变化。后一种观点仅仅抓住了这一命题的一半——即“万物不存在”。这完全不是赫拉克利特的本意。客观世界当然存在，但它处于永恒的运动、发展和变化之中，其中没有任何事物能保持原样。
en: They tried to use the arguments of Zeno and Heraclitus to justify their views, but did so in a negative and one-sided way. For example, Heraclitus had said that it is impossible to step in the same stream twice. One of his disciples went further, saying that you could not even step into it once! This, however, is false. The idea of Heraclitus was that everything is and is not, because everything is in flux, constantly changing. The second view merely takes one half of the equation – that everything is not. This is not at all what Heraclitus meant. The objective world certainly exists, but it is in a permanent process of motion, development and change, in which nothing remains as it was before.

zh: 智者学派是怀疑论者。普罗泰戈拉写道：
en: The sophists were sceptics. Protagoras wrote:

zh: 至于诸神，我无法断言他们是否存在；因为有许多因素阻碍着这种知识，既因事物的晦涩难明，也因人的生命如此短暂。
en: As to the gods, I am not able to say whether they are or are not; for there is much which prevents this knowledge, both in the obscurity of the matter, and in the life of man which is so short.

zh: 正是这句话导致他被逐出雅典。与早期哲学的根本区别在于智者派世界观的主观性。“人是万物的尺度”——这一论断可从实践和理论两个层面来理解。从第一层意义上说，它可被视为对利己主义、私利等观念的辩护；从第二层意义上说，它代表了一种主观的认识论。人将自身与客观世界对立起来，并至少在想象中将其置于自身掌控之下。他凭借自己的理性来判定事物的本质。关键不在于事物本身是什么，而在于我如何看待它。这是从普罗泰戈拉到贝克莱主教，从康德到维尔纳·海森堡，一切形式的主观唯心主义的基础。
en: That sentence got him banished from Athens. The fundamental difference with the earlier philosophy is the subjective character of the sophist outlook. “Man is the measure of all things” – this statement may be taken in two ways, practical and theoretical. In the first sense, it can be taken as a defence of egotism, self-interest, and the like. In the second sense, it represents a theory of knowledge (epistemology) which is subjective. Man counterposes himself to the objective world, and, at least in his imagination, subjects it to himself. His own reason decides what is what. The essential thing is not what is, but how I see it. This is the basis of all forms of subjective idealism, from Protagoras to Bishop Berkeley, from Kant to Werner Heisenberg.

zh: 从根本上说，主观唯心主义者主张世界是不可知的。我们无法真正把握真理，只能基于主观标准形成观点。“真理？”彼拉多讽刺地问道，“什么是真理？”这是玩世不恭的政治家和官僚的言辞，他们将自身利益隐藏在“有教养”的诡辩这层薄薄的遮羞布之后。然而从哲学角度而言，这正是主观唯心主义的体现，它否认了真正认识我们外部世界的可能性。这种观点最清晰地体现在最著名的智者之一——莱昂蒂尼的高尔吉亚（公元前483—375 年）身上，他写了一本标题颇具挑衅性的书：《论自然，或论那不存在之物》。书名本身已道尽一切。高尔吉亚的论点基于三个命题：a）没有任何事物是真实的；b）即使有事物是真实的，也无法被认知；c）即使能够被认知，也无法被表达。
en: Basically, the subjective idealist claims that the world is unknowable. We can have no real grasp of the truth, but only opinions, based on subjective criteria. “The truth?” asked Pontius Pilate ironically, “What is the truth?” That is the language of the cynical politician and bureaucrat, who hides his self-interest behind a thin veneer of ‘cultured’ sophistry. Philosophically speaking, however, it is an expression of subjective idealism, which denies the possibility of really knowing the world outside us. This outlook was most clearly expressed by one of the most famous sophists, Gorgias of Leontini (483-375 BC), who wrote a provocatively-titled book: On Nature, or On That Which Is Not. The title already says it all. Gorgias based himself on three propositions: a) nothing is real, b) if anything were real, it could not be known, and c) if it could be known, it could not be expressed.

zh: 这些观点看似荒谬。然而，它们在哲学史上却以各种形式反复出现，包括我们这个时代——即便是备受尊敬的科学家，也敢断言人类无法理解亚原子粒子的量子世界，并认为光子和电子只有在被某人观测时才会出现在特定位置；也就是说，观察者通过主观的观测行为创造了结果。在此，我们再次脱离了客观世界，并通过主观唯心主义的“后门”，回到了宗教神秘主义的领域。
en: Such opinions seem absurd. Yet they have repeatedly surfaced in the history of philosophy in different forms, including in our own times, when even respected scientists can permit themselves to assert that humans cannot comprehend the quantum world of subatomic particles, and that photons and electrons only materialise in a given spot when they are observed by someone; that is, the observer creates his result through the subjective act of observation. Here we once again depart from the world of objectivity, and return, through the tradesman’s entrance of subjective idealism, to the realms of religious mysticism.

zh: 当今主张此类观点的科学家，远不如智者们那样情有可原——那些智者毕竟是其所处时代的产物。早期为自然过程寻找理性解释的尝试，已达到仅凭思想无法再进一步的境地。那个时期的思想家们对宇宙的本质得出一系列精辟的概括。但为了检验并进一步发展这些概括，必须对其进行详细考察，将其分解为各个组成部分，逐一加以分析。这项工作由智者们开创，后来由亚里士多德将其建立在更严谨的基础上。伟大概括的英雄时代逐渐让位于对事实、实验和观察的缓慢而艰苦的积累。只有这样，才能最终证明各种假说的真伪。然而，在达到这一阶段之前，我们首先迎来了古典哲学唯心主义的高峰。
en: The present-day scientists who advocate such views have far less excuse than the sophists, who were the children of their time. The early attempts to find a rational explanation for the processes of nature had reached a point where they could not be taken any further by thought alone. The thinkers of that period arrived at a series of brilliant generalisations about the nature of the universe. But in order to test them and develop them further, it was necessary to examine them in detail, to break them down into their component parts, to analyse them one by one. This work was started by the sophists, and later put on a more rigorous basis by Aristotle. The heroic period of great generalisations gradually gave way to the slow and painstaking accumulation of facts, experiment and observation. Only in this way could the truth or falsehood of the different hypotheses be finally demonstrated. Before we reach this stage, however, we come to the high point of classical philosophical idealism.

zh: 苏格拉底与柏拉图
en: SOCRATES AND PLATO

zh: 智者们将客观世界从属于主观性，从而剥夺了客观世界的一切内在规律和必然性。秩序、理性与因果关系的唯一来源是感知的主体。一切都被宣称为相对的。例如，他们认为道德和社会行为取决于是否便利（实用主义者也持类似观点，这一哲学流派在美国曾广受支持，且与使道德与“自由企业”丛林法则相容的需求十分契合）。公元前5 世纪末，来自卡尔凯冬的色拉西马库斯公开宣称：“正义或权利，无非就是符合强者利益之事。”
en: By subordinating the objective world to subjectivity, the sophists had stripped it of all inherent law and necessity. The sole source of order, rationality and causation was the perceiving subject. Everything was declared to be relative. For example, they held that morality and social conduct was determined by convenience (a similar view is held by the Pragmatists, a philosophy which enjoyed a lot of support in the United States, and which fits in nicely with the need to make morality compatible with the ethics of the ‘free enterprise’ jungle). Thrasymachus of Chalcedon in the late fifth century BC openly declared that “justice or right is simply what is in the interest of the stronger party”.

zh: 这又是一个充满战争、革命与反革命的时期。公元前411 年，在经历了100 年的奴隶主民主制之后，雅典爆发了一场革命，两年后又发生了反政变。随后爆发了与斯巴达的灾难性战争，斯巴达强加了“三十僭主”的统治，执政的贵族派在此期间犯下了无数暴行。但到公元前399 年，“三十僭主”已被推翻，而苏格拉底——不幸的是，其中数人曾是他的学生和朋友——被送上法庭并判处死刑。
en: This was another period of war, revolution and counter-revolution. In 411 BC, after a 100 years of slave-owning democracy, there was a revolution in Athens, followed by a counter-coup two years later. There followed a disastrous war with Sparta, which imposed the rule of the ‘Thirty Tyrants’, under which numerous atrocities were perpetrated by the aristocratic party in power. But by 399 BC, the Thirty had been overthrown, and Socrates, who had the misfortune to have had several of them as his pupils and friends, was put on trial and sentenced to death.

zh: 苏格拉底（公元前469—399 年）虽未收取授课费用，却被同时代人视为智者。尽管他本人未留下任何著作——其思想是通过柏拉图和亚里士多德的著作流传至今的——但他对哲学的发展产生了巨大影响。他的出身卑微，父亲是石匠，母亲是助产士。他一生的驱动力是对追求真理的炽热渴望，通过无休止的问答过程，撕开一切伪装和诡辩。据说，为了引导人们思考普遍原理，他走遍工匠和商人的作坊，以及智者和年轻人的聚集地，对所有人采用同样的方法。
