en: Socrates (469-399 BC) was regarded by his contemporaries as a sophist, although he did not teach for money. Though he wrote nothing – his ideas have come down to us through the writings of Plato and Aristotle – he had a huge influence on the development of philosophy. His origins were humble; he was the son of a stonemason and a midwife. The driving force of his life was a burning desire to get at the truth, tearing aside all pretences and sophistry by a relentless process of question and answer. It is said that, in his attempt to get people to think about universal principles, he went about the workplaces of artisans and merchants, as well as the haunts of sophists and youths, subjecting all to the same procedure.

zh: 他的方法始终如一：从某个具体的想法或观点出发——通常源自当事人具体的生活经验和问题——他会通过一个严谨的论证，逐步揭示原命题所蕴含的内在矛盾，指出其局限性，并将讨论提升到更高层次，涉及一个截然不同的命题。这就是讨论中辩证法的经典形式。首先提出一个初始论点（正题），随后以相反的论点（反题）予以回应。最后，在对问题进行彻底考察、剖析以揭示其内在矛盾之后，我们便得出了更高层次的结论（合题）。这可能意味着双方达成一致，也可能并非如此。但在讨论发展的过程中，双方的理解都得到了深化，讨论也从较低层次提升到了较高层次。
en: The method was always the same: setting out from a particular idea or opinion, usually derived from the concrete experiences and problems of life of the person involved, he would, step-by-step, by a rigorous process of argument, bring to light the inner contradictions contained on the original proposition, show its limitations, and take the discussion to a higher level, involving an entirely different proposition. This is the dialectic of discussion in its classical form. An initial argument (thesis) is advanced. This is answered by a contrary argument (antithesis). Finally, after examining the question thoroughly, dissecting it to reveal its inner contradictions, we arrive at a conclusion on a higher level (synthesis). This may or may not mean that the two sides reach agreement. But in the very process of developing the discussion itself, the understanding of both sides is deepened, and the discussion proceeds from a lower to a higher level.

zh: 在科学和哲学史上，同样可以观察到这种通过矛盾发展思想的辩证过程。黑格尔在其开创性著作《精神现象学》的序言中对此作了生动的阐述：
en: The same dialectical process of the development of thought through contradiction can be seen in the history of science and philosophy. It was graphically expressed by Hegel in the Preface to his pioneering work The Phenomenology of Spirit:

zh: 花蕾在花朵绽放时便消失了，可以说花蕾被花朵所“驳倒”；同样，当果实出现时，花朵就被宣告为植物的一种虚假的定在［形式］，而果实则取代花朵，成为植物的真理。这些形式不仅不同，而且作为互不相容的形式而彼此取代。然而与此同时，它们流动的本质使它们成为有机统一体的各个环节，在其中它们不仅不相互冲突，而且彼此同样必要；而唯有这种共同的必要性，才构成了整体的生命。
en: The bud disappears when the blossom bursts forth, and one could say that the bud is refuted by the blossom; similarly, when the fruit appears, the blossom is declared to be a false Being-there [form] of the plant, and the fruit replaces the blossom as the truth of the plant. These forms are not only different, they also supplant one another as mutually incompatible. Yet at the same time their fluid nature makes them moments of the organic unity, in which they not only do not conflict, but each is as necessary as the other; and this shared necessity alone constitutes the life of the whole.

zh: 可以说，在苏格拉底的对话录中，我们虽未发现对辩证法的系统阐述，但确实发现了许多辩证方法付诸实践的重要实例。例如，著名的苏格拉底式反讽，并非仅仅是一种修辞手法，更是辩证法本身的体现。苏格拉底希望让他人意识到自己思想、信念和偏见背后潜藏的矛盾。对于每一个明确的命题，他都会直接推导出与该命题所述内容完全相反的结论。他并非仅仅攻击对手的观点，而是将他们置于一种境地，使他们自己得出相反的结论。这正是反讽的基础所在，不仅限于此处，更是普遍的规律。这种辩证讨论的艺术，是由苏格拉底臻于完美的。他本人将其比作助产术，并开玩笑说这是从母亲那里学来的。用黑格尔的话来说：
en: It is possible to say that in the Socratic dialogues we do not find a worked-out exposition of dialectics, but we do find many important examples of the dialectical method in action. The celebrated Socratic irony, for example, is not just a stylistic trick, but a reflection of the dialectic itself. Socrates wished to make other people become aware of the contradictions underlying their own ideas, beliefs and prejudices. From each definite proposition, he deduced as a direct result, the exact opposite of what the proposition stated. Instead of merely attacking his opponents’ ideas, he would put them in a position where they themselves would draw the opposite conclusion. This is precisely the basis of irony, not just here, but in general. This dialectic of discussion is an art which was perfected by Socrates. He himself likens it to the art of midwifery, which he jokingly claimed to have learnt from his mother. It is, to quote Hegel:

zh: ［将］已经蕴含在个体意识中的思想助其诞生——即从具体而未经反思的意识中，揭示具体事物的普遍性；或者从普遍地被设定的事物中，揭示其内部已经存在的对立面。
en: [T]he assisting into the world of the thought which is already contained in the consciousness of the individual – the showing from the concrete, unreflected consciousness, the universality of the concrete, or from the universally posited, the opposite which already is within it.

zh: 同样地，马克思主义者的任务并非像某些人想象的那样，从“外部”向工人阶级灌输社会主义意识，而是要从该阶级现有的意识状态出发，具体而逐步地展示：工人面临的问题唯有通过社会的根本性变革才能得到解决。这并非从外部进行说教，而是要使劳动人民改变社会的无意识愿望变得有意识。不同之处在于，这一过程并非仅在辩论厅中得以实现，而是通过实践活动、斗争以及该阶级自身的经验来实现的。尽管如此，问题本质上仍然相同：如何打破现有的偏见，让人们看到矛盾不仅存在于他们的脑海中，也存在于他们所生活的世界中——让他们看到事物的本来面目，而不是他们想象中的样子。
en: In just the same way, the task of Marxists is not to introduce into the working class a socialist consciousness ‘from without’, as some have imagined, but to proceed from the existing state of awareness of the class, and show concretely, step-by-step, how the problems which workers face can only be resolved by a radical transformation of society. It is not a question of preaching from without, but of making conscious the unconscious aspiration of working people to change society. The difference is that this process is not brought to fruition exclusively in the debating chamber, but by practical activity, struggle and the experience of the class itself. The problem, nevertheless, remains essentially the same: how to break down existing prejudices and get people to see the contradictions present, not only in their heads, but in the world in which they live – to get them to see things as they really are, not as they imagine them to be.

zh: 苏格拉底会从我们感官所感知到的最显而易见、最日常、甚至最琐碎的事实入手。然后，他会将这些事实与其他事实进行比较，从一个细节推向另一个细节，以此方式逐步剔除所有偶然的和次要的方面，直到最终使我们直面问题的本质。这就是归纳法，即从特殊推向普遍，这是科学发展中至关重要的一种方法。亚里士多德明确将归纳法及其密切相关的逻辑定义的发明（或至少是完善）归功于苏格拉底。
en: Socrates would begin with the most self-evident, everyday, even trivial facts given to us by our senses. Then he would compare these with other facts, proceeding from one detail to the next, and in this way, gradually eliminating all accidental and secondary aspects, until, finally, we are brought face to face with the essence of the question. This is the method of induction, proceeding from the particular to the universal, a most important method for the development of science. Aristotle explicitly credits Socrates with the invention (or, at least, perfection) of the method of induction and logical definitions which are closely related to it.

zh: 探索隐藏在个别事物之中的普遍性，是人类思想发展过程中最重要的方面之一。从记录个别事实和情境的初级感官知觉出发，人的思维开始缓慢而艰难地从这些个别事物中进行抽象，剔除非本质的部分，直至最终得出一系列或多或少抽象的概括。尽管这些“普遍性”无法脱离体现它们的具体事物而独立存在，但它们确实代表了事物的本质，表达了比具体事物更深邃、更深刻的真理。人类思想的总体进步，与基于经验进行概括、并得出符合现实本质的抽象观念的能力密切相关。
en: The search for the general which lies hidden within the particular is one of the most important aspects of the development of human thought in general. Starting with elementary sense perception which registers individual facts and circumstances, the human mind begins slowly and painfully to abstract from these particulars, discarding the inessential, until it finally arrives at a series of more or less abstract generalisations. Though these ‘universals’ have no existence separate and apart from the particular things that embody them, they nonetheless represent the essential being of things, expressing a far deeper and more profound truth than the particular. The progress of human thought in general is closely related to the ability to generalise on the basis of experience, and to arrive at abstract ideas which correspond to the nature of reality.

zh: 托洛茨基在他的自传中曾提及这个问题：
en: In his autobiography, Trotsky touches on this question:

zh: 后来，一般性优于特殊性的这种感觉，成了我文学和政治工作不可或缺的一部分。那种呆板的经验主义，那种对事实毫不掩饰、卑躬屈膝的崇拜——这些事实往往只是虚构的，甚至被错误解读的事实，都令我深恶痛绝。在事实之外，我寻求的是规律。自然，这曾不止一次地使我陷入草率且错误的概括，特别是在我年轻的时候，那时我从书本上获得的知识和生活经验还远远不够。但在每一个领域，无一例外，我都感到只有当我掌握了普遍性的线索时，才能前进和行动。
en: Later, the feeling of the supremacy of the general over the particular became an integral part of my literary and political work. The dull empiricism, the unashamed, cringing worship of the fact which is so often only imaginary, and falsely interpreted at that, were odious to me. Beyond the facts, I looked for laws. Naturally, this led me more than once into hasty and incorrect generalisations, especially in my younger years when my knowledge, book-acquired, and my experience in life were still inadequate. But in every sphere, barring none, I felt that I could move and act only when I held in my hand the thread of the general.

zh: 苏格拉底的目标是通过逻辑论证，从特殊推向一般，从而抵达“普遍”。对他而言，这已不再是像早期希腊哲学家那样去探求支配自然的最普遍规律，而是让人去审视自己、自己的本性、自己的思想和行为。苏格拉底的哲学不是自然哲学，而是社会哲学，尤其是伦理与道德哲学。他最关注的问题是“什么是善？”实际上，这个问题只能结合社会的历史发展来具体回答，因为根本不存在超历史的道德。这一点在古希腊的案例中表现得尤为明显，那里的语言本身就暴露了道德的历史相对性。希腊语中表示“善”的词“arete”，与其拉丁语对应词“virtus”（英语“virtue”即由此衍生）一样，最初意指一种好斗的男子气概。正如J. D. 伯纳尔所指出的：“它花了很长时间才逐渐软化为公民理想的温和形态，而转变为基督教顺从的形态则耗时更久。”
en: The aim of Socrates was to proceed, by means of logical argumentation, from the particular to the general, to arrive at the ‘universal’. For him, this was no longer a question of getting to the most general laws governing nature, as was the case with earlier Greek philosophers, but rather of man examining himself, his own nature, his thought and actions. The philosophy of Socrates is not the philosophy of nature but the philosophy of society, above all of ethics and morality. His favourite subject is ‘what is the Good?’ In reality, this question can only be answered concretely, with reference to the historical development of society, since there is no such thing as a supra-historical morality. This can be seen clearly in the case of ancient Greece, where the very language betrays the historical relativity of morality. The Greek word for goodness ‘arete’, like its Latin equivalent, ‘virtus’ (from which we get the English ‘virtue’) originally meant something like combative manliness. As J. D. Bernal points out: “It took a long time to soften into the ideal of citizenship and still longer to Christian submissiveness.”

zh: 尽管如此，重要的并非这些对话的主题，而是其方法。这实际上标志着逻辑学的诞生，逻辑学最初就是对词语（希腊语“logoi”）的处理。因此，逻辑与辩证法原本是一回事——一种探求真理的技术。该方法涉及将概念分解为构成部分，揭示其内在矛盾，然后将其重新组合。这是一个动态的过程，甚至带有某种戏剧性和意外性。当发现先前持有的观念中存在根本性矛盾时，最初的反应往往是惊讶。例如，运动意味着同时在同一地点而又不在这一地点这一观念。辩证法不断挑战那些乍看之下似乎无可置疑的观点。它揭示了庸俗思维、“常识”以及对“事实”的肤浅诉求的局限性——正如托洛茨基正确指出的那样，这些“事实”往往只是虚构的，且被错误地解释了。
en: Nonetheless, what is important is not the subject matter of these dialogues, but the method. This really represents the birth of logic, which was originally the handling of words (Greek ‘logoi’). Thus, logic and dialectics were originally the same – a technique for getting at the truth. The method involved breaking up concepts into their constituent parts, revealing their inner contradictions, and putting them back together again. It was a dynamic process, with even a certain element of drama and surprise. The first reaction to the discovery of a fundamental contradiction in previously held ideas is one of surprise. For example, the idea that motion implies being and not being in the same place at the same time. The dialectic constantly challenges what appeared at first sight to be unquestionable. It shows the limitations of vulgar thinking, ‘common sense’ and superficial appeals to the ‘facts’, which, as Trotsky rightly remarked, are so often only imaginary, and falsely interpreted.

zh: 超越个别现象、分解感官所提供的信息并得出抽象概括的任务，是人类思想发展与成长的根基，这不仅体现在历史层面上，也体现在每个个体从童年走向自觉成熟的艰辛奋斗过程中。在柏拉图（公元前428—348年）的著作中，对普遍性、对“普遍概念”的追寻成为了哲学的核心议题，排斥了一切其他内容，甚至可以说几乎成了一种执念。在这些著作中，深刻的思想、灿烂的文风以及辩证讨论中的一些精妙范例，与人类思想所产生过的最赤裸裸、最令人费解的唯心主义交织在一起。
en: The task of going beyond the particular, of breaking down the information provided by our eyes and ears, and arriving at abstract generalisations lies at the root of the development and growth of human thought, not only in a historical sense, but in the evolution of every individual in the arduous struggle to pass from childhood to conscious maturity. In the writings of Plato (428-348 BC) the search for the general, the ‘universal’, becomes the central issue of philosophy to the exclusion of all else, one might say almost an obsession. In these works, profound thoughts, a brilliant style and some masterly examples of the dialectic of discussion are mixed up with the most blatant and mystifying idealism ever produced by the human mind.

zh: 对柏拉图而言，思想中的普遍性——例如“圆”的理念——具有独立的存在，与具体的圆形物体相互分离、独立于它们。正如我们所见，从唯物主义的角度来看，“圆”的理念最初源于对圆形物体长期观察的积累。但柏拉图却不这么认为。如果观察任何一个圆形物体的实例——例如这张桌子上的盘子——就会发现它并不完美。因此，它仅仅是世界开天辟地之前就已存在的完美圆的拙劣复制品。对于一群习惯于仅在思想和语言中进行活动的富裕知识分子来说，这些思想和语言在他们眼中似乎具有自身生命和力量，这在逻辑上是合乎情理的：
en: For Plato, the universals of thought, for example, the idea of a circle, had an independent existence, separate and apart from particular round objects. From a materialist standpoint, as we have seen, the idea of a circle was originally derived from the observation of round objects over a long period of time. Not so, says Plato. If one looks at any example of a round object, for instance the plate on this table, it will be seen to be imperfect. It is therefore only a poor copy of the perfect circle that existed before the world began. For a class of wealthy intellectuals, used to working only with thoughts and words, it was logical that these should appear to them to be endowed with a life and a power of their own:

zh: 对词语及其真实含义的强调，往往赋予词语一种独立于其所指事物和行为的现实性。既然有“美”这个词，那么“美”本身就必须是真实的。事实上，它必须比任何美丽的事物都更真实。这是因为没有任何美丽的事物是完全美丽的，因此它是否美丽只是见仁见智的问题；而“美”本身除了自身之外别无他物，必须独立于这个变化无常且不完美的物质世界而存在。同样的逻辑也适用于具体事物：一般意义上的“石头”必然比任何特定的石头更真实。
en: The emphasis on the discussion of words and their true meanings tended to give to words a reality independent of the things and actions to which they referred. Because there is a word for beauty, beauty itself must be real. Indeed it must be more real than any beautiful thing. This is because no beautiful thing is altogether beautiful, and so whether it is beautiful or not is a matter of opinion, whereas beauty contains nothing but itself and must exist independently of anything in this changing and imperfect material world. The same logic applies to concrete things: a stone in general must be more real than any particular stone.

zh: 柏拉图的唯心主义
en: PLATO’S IDEALISM

zh: 在《斐多篇》中，柏拉图系统地阐述了这一思想。如果我们追问事物的成因，最终将抵达其本质——希腊语称之为“eidos”，可译为“形式”或“理念”，尽管亚里士多德将其解释为“种”，从唯物主义的角度来看，后者显然更可取。回到我们的餐盘，是什么让它呈圆形？或者——用柏拉图的语言来说——它圆形的根源是什么？有人可能会回答：是因为陶工在转轮上旋转一团黏土，并用手将其塑形。但对柏拉图而言，餐盘与所有其他粗糙的物质对象一样，仅仅是“理念”的一种不完美的体现；通俗地说，这个“理念”就是上帝。
en: In his work Phaedo, Plato develops this idea in a consistent way. If we ask what the cause of a thing is, we end up with its essence – the Greek word is ‘eidos’, which can be variously translated as form or idea, although Aristotle interprets it as ‘species’, which is obviously preferable from a materialist standpoint. To go back to our dinner plate, what makes it round? Or – to use Platonic language – what is the cause of its roundness? One might answer: that it was caused by a potter rotating a lump of clay on a wheel and moulding it with his hand. But for Plato, the plate, like all other crude material objects, is merely an imperfect manifestation of the Idea, which, put in plain language, is God.

zh: 柏拉图的知识论——亚里士多德认为它与苏格拉底的知识论不同——基于这样一种观点：知识的对象必须是恒久、永恒的；既然世间万物皆非恒久，我们就必须在这个转瞬即逝且虚幻的物质世界之外寻求稳定的知识。当第欧根尼嘲讽“理念论”时，他说自己能看见杯子，却看不见“杯性”，柏拉图反驳道，那是因为他虽有眼睛能看，却缺乏理性。确实，仅凭感官知觉是不够的。必须从个别走向普遍。这里的基本谬误在于认为，理性的概括可以独立存在，脱离并对抗于物质世界——而这些概括归根结底正是源自物质世界。
en: Plato’s theory of knowledge, which Aristotle says is different from that of Socrates, was based on the idea that the object of knowledge must be permanent, eternal, and since nothing under the sun is permanent, we must seek stable knowledge outside this fleeting and deceitful world of material things. When Diogenes ridiculed the theory of Ideas, by saying he could see the cup, but not ‘cupness’, Plato retorted that that was because he had eyes to see, but no intellect. And it is true that merely to base oneself on sense-perception is not enough. It is necessary to go from the particular to the universal. The fundamental flaw here is to think that the generalisations of the intellect can stand on their own, divorced from, and counterposed to, the material world from which, ultimately, they are derived.

zh: 马克思和恩格斯在《神圣家族》中解释道：在唯心主义哲学中，思想与存在之间的真实关系被彻底颠倒了：
en: Marx and Engels, in The Holy Family, explained: in the philosophy of Idealism, the real relations between thought and being are stood on their head:

zh: ［对］绝对唯心主义者而言，为了成为绝对唯心主义者，就必然必须不断经历这样一个诡辩过程：首先将自身之外的世界转化为一种表象——即大脑中的一种纯粹幻想；随后又宣称这种幻想正是其真实本质，即一种纯粹的幻想；最终才能宣称其唯一且排他的存在，这种存在甚至不再受到外部世界的表象的干扰。
en: [F]or the absolute idealist, in order to be an absolute idealist, must necessarily constantly go through the sophistical process of first transforming the world outside himself into an appearance, a mere fancy of his brain, and afterwards declaring this fantasy to be what it really is, i.e., a mere fantasy, so as finally to be able to proclaim his sole, exclusive existence, which is no longer disturbed even by the semblance of an external world.

zh: 同一著作中机智地阐明了实现这一目的的诡辩伎俩：
en: The sophistical trick whereby this is done was wittily explained in the same work:

zh: 如果我从真实的苹果、梨、草莓和杏仁中形成“果实”这一普遍概念，如果我更进一步，设想这个源自真实水果的抽象概念“果实”是一个存在于我之外的实体，确实是梨、苹果等的真实本质，那么——在思辨哲学的语言中——我便是在宣称“果实”是梨、苹果、杏仁等的“实体”。因此，我是在说：是一个梨这一点对梨而言并非本质性的，是一个苹果这一点对苹果而言也非本质性的；对这些事物而言，其本质并非感官所能感知到的真实存在，而是我从它们身上抽象出来并强加给它们的本质，即我观念中的本质——“果实”。因此，我宣称苹果、梨、杏仁等不过是“果实”的单纯存在形式（modi）。我那依靠感官支撑的有限知性，当然能将苹果与梨区分开来，将梨与杏仁区分开来，但我的思辨理性却宣称这些感性差异是非本质的、无关紧要的。它在苹果中看到与在梨中看到的一样，在梨中看到与在杏仁中看到的一样，即“果实”。个别真实的果实不过是表象，其真正的本质是“实体”——“果实”。
en: If from real apples, pears, strawberries and almonds I form the general idea ‘Fruit’, if I go further and imagine that my abstract idea ‘Fruit’, derived from real fruit, is an entity existing outside me, is indeed the true essence of the pear, the apple, etc., then – in the language of speculative philosophy – I am declaring that ‘Fruit’ is the ‘Substance’ of the pear, the apple, the almond, etc. I am saying, therefore, that to be a pear is not essential to the pear, that to be an apple is not essential to the apple; that what is essential to these things is not their real existence, perceptible to the senses, but the essence that I have abstracted from them and then foisted on them, the essence of my idea – ‘Fruit’. I therefore declare apples, pears, almonds, etc., to be mere forms of existence, modi, of ‘Fruit’. My finite understanding supported by my senses does of course distinguish an apple from a pear and a pear from an almond, but my speculative reason declares these sensuous differences inessential and irrelevant. It sees in the apple the same as in the pear, and in the pear the same as in the almond, namely ‘Fruit’. Particular real fruits are no more than semblances whose true essence is “the substance” – ‘Fruit’.

zh: 唯心主义的方法非但未能促进人类理性的发展，甚至未能让我们向前迈进一步。唯有对现实的——即物质世界——的研究，才能加深我们对自然及我们在其中的位置的理解。唯心主义者将人们的目光从“粗鄙”的物质事物转向所谓的“纯粹”抽象领域，几个世纪以来严重阻碍了科学的发展。
en: Far from advancing the cause of human understanding, the idealist method does not take us a single step forward. Only a study of the real, that is to say, material world, can deepen our understanding of nature and our place in it. By directing men’s eyes away from ‘crude’ material things towards the realm of so-called ‘pure’ abstraction, the idealists played havoc with the development of science for centuries.

zh: 通过这种方法，无法获得任何丰富的具体规定。如果一位矿物学家的研究仅限于断言“所有矿物实际上都是‘矿物’”，那么他充其量只是在想象中才算得上矿物学家。对于每一种矿物，这种思辨式的矿物学家都称之为“矿物”，而他的“科学”也就沦为将这个词重复多少次，就等于有多少种真实的矿物。
en: By this method one attains no particular wealth of definition. The mineralogist whose science was limited to the statement that all minerals are really ‘the Mineral’ would be a mineralogist only in his imagination. For every mineral the speculative mineralogist says ‘the Mineral’, and his science is reduced to repeating this word as many times as there are real minerals.

zh: 与早期希腊哲学家不同——他们大多是唯物主义者，并以研究自然为出发点——柏拉图有意识地背离了感官世界。通往真理的道路不是实验和观察，而是纯粹的演绎和数学。他在雅典学园的入口上方刻下铭文：“凡不懂几何者，不得入内。”例如，柏拉图鼓励他的学生研究星辰，不是研究它们的实际状态，而是研究它们“理应”有的状态。他追随毕达哥拉斯学派的脚步，声称行星通过其永恒不变的轨道展现了神圣的本质，其圆周运动的完美规律性正是宇宙和谐的体现。这种宇宙论，连同他的伟大继任者亚里士多德的宇宙论，在2000年间阻碍了天文学的发展。它标志着科学向毕达哥拉斯神秘主义的倒退。因此，在盖米努斯所著的亚历山大里亚天文学手册中，我们读到：
en: As opposed to the earlier Greek philosophers, who were generally materialists and set out from a study of nature, Plato consciously turned his back on the world of the senses. Not experiment and observation, but only pure deduction and mathematics was the road to truth. Above the entrance of his Academy in Athens he placed the inscription: “Let no man destitute of geometry enter my doors.” Plato encouraged his students, for example, to study the stars, not as they are, but as they ought to be. Following in the footsteps of the Pythagoreans, he alleged that the planets showed their divine nature by their eternally unchanging orbits, the perfect regularity of their circular motion being an expression of the harmony of the universe. This cosmology, together with that of Aristotle, his great successor, held back the development of astronomy for 2,000 years. It represented a retreat from science to Pythagorean mysticism. Thus, in an Alexandrian handbook on astronomy written by Geminus, we read:

zh: 整个天文学的根基……在于这样一个假设：太阳、月亮和五颗行星以恒定速度沿完美的圆周运动，其方向与宇宙的运转方向相反。正是最早探讨这些问题的毕达哥拉斯学派，提出了太阳、月亮和行星作圆周匀速运动的假说。他们认为，对于神圣而永恒的存在而言，假设这些天体时快时慢，甚至停滞不动——正如所谓的“行星停滞”现象——是不可接受的。即便在人类领域，这种不规则性也与绅士有条不紊的行事方式不相容。而且，即使粗鄙的生活必需常常迫使人们不得不匆忙或拖延，也不能认为此类情况存在于恒星那不朽的本质之中。正因如此，他们将研究问题界定为：在圆周匀速运动的假设下解释这些现象。
en: There underlies the whole science of astronomy… the assumption that the sun and the moon and the five planets move at even speeds in perfect circles in an opposite direction to the cosmos. It was the Pythagoreans, the first to approach these questions, who laid down the hypothesis of a circular and uniform motion for the sun, moon, and planets. Their view was that, in regard of divine and eternal beings, a supposition of such disorder as that these bodies should move now more quickly and now more slowly, or should even stop, as in what are called the stations of the planets, is inadmissible. Even in the human sphere such irregularity is incompatible with the orderly procedure of a gentleman. And even if the crude necessities of life often impose upon men occasions of haste or loitering, it is not to be supposed that such occasions inhere in the incorruptible nature of the stars. For this reason they defined their problem as the explanation of the phenomena on the hypothesis of circular and uniform motion.

zh: 开普勒发现，行星的运动轨迹并非圆形，而是椭圆形。正如牛顿后来所证明的，这一发现也并非完全正确。这些椭圆轨迹本身也并非完美无缺。但在此前两千年的时间里，这种唯心主义的宇宙图景却具有着无可置疑的教条般的权威。在此期间的大部分时间里，它还得到了教会那股强大势力的支持。
en: Kepler discovered that the planets moved, not in circles, but in ellipses. Even this was not completely true, as Newton later showed. The ellipses are not perfect, either. But for the previous two millennia, the idealist picture of the universe held the force of an unchallengeable dogma. For much of that time it was backed by the formidable power of the Church.

zh: 值得注意的是，在中世纪，人们仅通过柏拉图的一部著作——《蒂迈欧篇》（他最差的一部著作）——来了解他的思想。这标志着哲学领域的一场彻底的反革命。从泰勒斯开始，希腊哲学的特点就是试图用自然的因素来解释世界，而不诉诸神灵或任何超自然现象。《蒂迈欧篇》并非哲学著作，而是一篇宗教小册子。正如马克思曾言，我们在此看到“全部陈旧的垃圾”的死灰复燃。实际上，这是对古老创世神话的复兴。世界是由一位至高无上的工匠创造的。物质由三角形构成，因为立体由平面界定，而平面可以分解为三角形。
en: It is significant that the ideas of Plato were known in the Middle Ages through only one work, The Timaeus, his worst book. This represents a complete counter-revolution in philosophy. From Thales on, Greek philosophy was characterised by an attempt to explain the world in natural terms, without recourse to the gods or any supernatural phenomena. The Timaeus is not a work of philosophy but a religious tract. Here we see a revival of “all the old crap”, as Marx once put it. It is, in effect, the revival of the old creation myth. The world was created by a Supreme Craftsman. Matter consists of triangles because solids are bounded by planes, and planes can be resolved into triangles.

zh: 世界呈球体并沿圆周运动，因为圆形是最完美的形态。行为不端的男人在下一世会转世为女性，诸如此类。
en: The world is spherical and moves in circles because the circle is the most perfect form. Men who live badly are reborn as women in the next reincarnation, and so on and so forth.

zh: 在一段与当今“大爆炸”理论支持者的某些论述惊人相似的段落中，柏拉图这样描述“时间的开端”：
en: In a passage strikingly similar to some of the statements of the present-day defenders of the ‘big bang’, Plato writes about the ‘beginning of time’:

zh: 因此，时间与天穹在同一瞬间诞生，以便它们既然一同被创造，倘若将来有解体之日，它们便能一同消亡。它是按照永恒本性的模式构筑的，以便尽可能地与之相似；因为该模式自永恒以来便存在，而被创造的苍穹在所有时间里都曾存在、正在存在并将继续存在。这就是上帝在创造时间时的意念与思想。
en: Time, then, and the heaven came into being at the same instant in order that, having been created together, if ever there was to be a dissolution of them, they might be dissolved together. It was framed after the pattern of the eternal nature, that it might resemble this as far as was possible; for the pattern exists from eternity, and the created heaven has been, and is, and will be, in all time. Such was the mind and thought of God in the creation of time.

zh: 难怪基督教会会张开双臂欣然接纳这一思想！
en: No wonder the Christian Church welcomed this with open arms!

zh: 尽管具有辩证的一面，柏拉图哲学本质上仍是一种保守的哲学，反映了贵族精英的世界观——他们正确地感觉到，他们所处的世界正在分崩离析。背离现实、否认感官所见、在动荡与剧变中执着于某种稳定、否定变化——所有这些都显然满足了一种强烈的心理和道德需求。
en: Despite its dialectical side, the Platonic philosophy is essentially a conservative one, reflecting the world outlook of an aristocratic elite, who felt, correctly, that their world was crumbling about them. The urge to turn one’s back on reality, to deny the evidence of one’s senses, to cling to some kind of stability in the midst of turbulence and upheaval, to deny change, all this clearly corresponded to a powerful psychological and moral need.
